title: Evaluation of FatNav-Based Prospective Motion Correction for Perivascular Space Imaging With T2-Weighted MRI at 7 T.
abstract: Subject motion during MRI acquisition is one of the major factors limiting image quality and diagnostic value. Previous studies have demonstrated the effectiveness of prospective motion correction (PMC) in mitigating motion-related artifacts. However, the effectiveness of PMC for the visualization of perivascular spaces (PVS) has not yet been systematically evaluated in clinical populations. PVS imaging was performed using a T2-weighted 3D turbo spin echo (TSE) sequence with fat navigator (FatNav)-based PMC. Ten healthy participants were scanned with and without PMC while performing gradual instructed motion. To further evaluate the effectiveness of PMC in a clinical setting, 62 patients were scanned after being instructed to keep their heads still. Among them, 28 patients underwent paired PMC-on and PMC-off scans, whereas 34 patients underwent PMC-on scans only. The degree of motion and its impact on overall image quality was assessed by two experienced radiologists using a 4-point Likert scale. Quantitative metrics were further evaluated including structural similarity index measure (SSIM), peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), PVS count, PVS volume, and contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) between PVS and neighboring tissue. The motion scores were significantly larger in subjects with instructed motion than in patients with involuntary motion (10.3 ± 5.3 mm vs. 1.47 ± 0.97 mm). For instructed motion, PMC significantly improved visual scores and quantitative metrics and weakened negative correlations between motion and the metrics. For involuntary motion, PMC significantly increased CNR (p < 0.001) and attenuated negative correlations between visual score and motion severity. The improvement in PVS CNR after PMC correlated strongly with motion score ( ρ = 0.40, p = 0.04). However, no significant difference was observed in PVS count and volume between images with and without PMC. In conclusion, FatNav-based PMC improved the motion robustness of 3D TSE images and PVS quantification in the presence of substantial motion, whereas its benefits for small involuntary motion appeared to be limited.

title: Optimal Control-Based RF Pulses Versus Classical Motion-Encoding Strategies for In Vivo Hepatic MR Elastography Across Multiple Excitation Frequencies in Mice: Reproducibility Assessment.
abstract: This study compared an optimal control (OC)-based motion-encoding approach using radiofrequency (RF) pulses with the conventional motion-encoding gradient (MEG) method for in vivo hepatic magnetic resonance elastography (MRE) across multiple excitation frequencies in mice, evaluating signal quality and temporal reproducibility. Eight healthy C57BL/6 mice, including four males and four females, underwent hepatic MRE at 7T at 300, 500 and 600 Hz using RARE-based sequences: classical MEG-MRE and optimized OC-MRE with GRAPE-designed RF pulses. In both sequences, motion was encoded only along the slice direction. Each mouse was scanned on days 1, 15 and 90. Reconstruction involved phase unwrapping, directional filtering and inversion with the Algebraic Inversion of Differential Equation algorithm to estimate the shear storage modulus ( G' ) on the manual liver segmentation and on an automatic circular region of interest designed for statistical analyses. Signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), phase-to-noise ratio (PNR) and intra/interanimal reproducibility were quantified using ANOVA, intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC), Bland-Altman analysis and coefficients of variation (CV). OC-MRE provided a mean twofold increase in SNR compared with MEG-MRE (OC/MEG = 1.8-2.1 across frequencies) and higher PNR values. G' increased with frequency for both methods, consistent with viscoelastic behavior and showed strong intermethod agreement (mean bias < 0.05 kPa; r > 0.96, p < 0.001). Intra-animal reproducibility was moderate at 300 Hz (ICC = 0.31-0.50) and high at 500-600 Hz (ICC > 0.75). No significant temporal changes in hepatic stiffness were observed across sessions. OC-MRE improves signal quality while maintaining quantitative consistency with conventional MEG-MRE. Its short echo time and absence of motion encoding gradients enhance robustness and make it a promising tool for longitudinal small-animal studies and future clinical translation, particularly in scenarios with short transverse relaxation times ( T2 / T2* ) such as those encountered in hepatic iron overload.

title: A Reproducible MRI-Based Pipeline for Longitudinal Tracking of Laser-Assisted Bioprinted Cells in Three-Dimensional Constructs.
abstract: Laser-assisted bioprinting (LAB) enables precise spatial patterning of living cells within three-dimensional constructs; however, the lack of non-destructive, standardised methods for longitudinal evaluation remains a major limitation to construct optimisation and translation. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) offers unique advantages for volumetric and repeated imaging due to its non-invasiveness, yet its application to complex multilayer bioprinted constructs has not been systematically assessed using quantitative workflows. In this study, we developed and evaluated an MRI-based pipeline for the longitudinal tracking and quantitative analysis of laser-assisted bioprinted cells within three-dimensional constructs of increasing architectural complexity. Iron oxide-labelled endothelial cells were bioprinted onto gelatin-based biopapers in predefined patterns and assembled into constructs composed of three, six or nine stacked layers. Constructs were monitored at 4.7 T using a high-resolution three-dimensional steady-state free precession sequence for up to 35 days, and quantitative image analysis was independently performed by three operators using the open-source 3D Slicer image computing platform. MRI enabled clear visualisation of printed patterns and multilayer architectures over time due to the signal drop induced by iron oxide particles. Quantitative analysis demonstrated high inter-operator reproducibility and revealed construct thickness-dependent differences in volume and signal-to-noise ratio. As a proof of concept, stacked bioprinted constructs were additionally visualised post-mortem in a murine calvarial defect model, enabling discrimination of individual layers and printed patterns. Together, these results establish MRI as a robust, non-destructive tool for the longitudinal evaluation of complex laser-assisted bioprinted constructs.

title: MR Derived Cardiac Metabolism Changes in Patients With Obesity and Diabetes: Knowledge Discovery Via Bayesian Networks and Random Forest Classification.
abstract: Recent developments in magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS) techniques have demonstrated great potential for the quantification of myocardial energy metabolites, enabling an in-depth glimpse into the energetic state of the heart to better explain the onset and severity of disease states. However, more evidence is required to establish its clinical impact and explanatory power compared to other diagnostic variables. In this study, random forest classification was used on data from 195 subjects to discriminate between healthy vs. obese non-diabetic, healthy vs. diabetic, healthy vs. non-obese diabetic, obese non-diabetic vs. obese diabetic, and non-obese diabetic vs. obese diabetic patient subgroups using 31 P-MRS and 1 H-MRS measurements of cardiac energetics, along with MRI measures of cardiac function, fat volumes, blood pressure, and blood glucose and cholesterol levels. Achieving 78.12%, 88.57%, 85.19%, 90.48%, and 76.47% test accuracies, SHAPs (SHapley Additive exPlanations) feature importances indicate a higher predictive impact of metabolic metrics for classifying the diabetic heart compared to global function metrics, gained through most common imaging techniques. Bayesian networks generated through structure learning of the data further suggests a potential causal association of increased visceral fat, increased LVMass resulting in decreased PCr/ATP, and increased cardiac lipid levels attributed to these disease states. Through the results, we have been able to showcase the importance of MRS measurements, both as strong features separating the diseases with clinically-relevant accuracy and furthermore its causal connection to other cardiac parameters.

title: MRpro: Open Framework for Model-Based, Learned, and Quantitative MR Imaging-Application to Low-Field MRI.
abstract: MRpro is an open-source framework for MR image reconstruction and quantitative parameter estimation, with particular relevance to low-field MRI. Built on PyTorch, it supports modern deep-learning reconstructions and standardized data exchange through ISMRMRD for raw k-space data and DICOM and NIfTI for reconstructed images and parameter maps. This facilitates integration into existing pipelines and the use of data from different devices. MRpro provides unified data structures for the consistent manipulation of MR datasets and associated metadata, together with a library of composable operators, proximable functionals, and optimization algorithms. The operator library includes a unified Fourier operator for all common trajectories and operators specifically developed for low-field applications, such as a B 0 -correction operator. Together, these components underpin ready-to-use implementations of key reconstruction algorithms. For deep learning, MRpro includes data-consistency layers, differentiable optimization layers, state-of-the-art backbone networks, and access to public datasets to facilitate reproducibility. Automated quality control supports collaborative development. We demonstrate MRpro for automatic reconstruction, iterative SENSE, deep-learning-based reconstruction, and quantitative parameter estimation. For selected Cartesian and non-Cartesian tasks, iterative SENSE reconstructions from MRpro differed from those obtained with BART, SigPy, and MRIReco by less than 3% relative RMSE. Further applications use public and simulated datasets and measured low-field data acquired at 0.3 T, 0.6 T, and 47 mT. MRpro provides a reproducible and maintainable foundation for future MR imaging research.

title: Radial Tiny Golden Angle UTE (tyGA-UTE) for Cardiac MRI in the Small Animal Model.
abstract: Robust cardiorespiratory motion correction is critical for high-quality ultra-high-field (UHF) preclinical cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Whereas radial tiny golden angle (tyGA) sampling, data-driven self-gating (sg), compressed sensing (CS), and ultrashort echo time (UTE) are individually well-established techniques, their integration into a unified acquisition and reconstruction pipeline, together with systematic validation at 11.7 T remains insufficiently explored. This study presents and validates a UHF-optimized tyGA-based UTE workflow that enables high-temporal-resolution sliding-window dynamic imaging (SW-tyGA-UTE) and high-spatial-resolution cardiorespiratory self-gated cine imaging (Gated-tyGA-UTE) from a single continuous acquired tyGA acquisition. All experiments were performed on an 11.7-T small-animal MRI system in 16 healthy wild-type mice. Cardiac functional parameters, image quality metrics (signal-to-noise ratio [SNR] and contrast-to-noise ratio [CNR]), and inter-/intra-observer reproducibility were systematically compared between the proposed tyGA-UTE pipeline and two navigator-gated reference techniques: retrospectively gated FLASH and UTE methodologies. SW-tyGA-UTE and Gated-tyGA-UTE reconstructions yielded global left ventricular functional parameters comparable to those obtained with the reference methods (all p > 0.05). All functional metrics showed excellent intra-observer (ICC = 0.94-0.99) and inter-observer (ICC = 0.90-0.98) reproducibility, with ejection fraction showing the highest measurement consistency. Image quality was evaluated using an image-based within-ROI noise quantification approach that captures both thermal noise and reconstruction-related artifacts. In this analysis, the Gated-tyGA-UTE protocol showed no statistically significant differences in left ventricular blood-pool SNR, myocardial SNR, or CNR relative to the reference sequences. In contrast, the high-temporal-resolution sliding-window reconstruction showed significantly reduced image quality across all three metrics, consistent with the expected spatiotemporal trade-off of undersampled dynamic imaging. This study validates a robust, UHF-optimized tyGA-UTE imaging workflow that generates both high-fidelity quantitative cine data and ultra-fast dynamic cardiac images from a single acquisition. The unified pipeline eliminates the need for sequential repeated scans, minimizes anesthesia-related physiological variability, and improves experimental efficiency, providing a practical tool for preclinical cardiac phenotyping, longitudinal studies, and drug screening.

title: Volumetric and Intrastructural Characterization of the Substantia Nigra Using Optimized Synthetic MR Images Derived From Quantitative T1 Maps at 3 T.
abstract: Accurate imaging of the substantia nigra (SN) is critical for diagnosing and monitoring neurodegenerative conditions like Parkinson's disease. However, conventional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) struggles to precisely visualize this small structure within the deep brain due to poor intrinsic tissue contrast. Although quantitative MRI (qMRI) captures objective tissue properties with diagnostic value to assess neurodegenerative conditions of the SN, additionally acquiring multiple MRI contrasts inherently requires impractically long scan times. To overcome this, qMRI-derived synthetic MRI uses mathematical signal models to retrospectively generate various synthetic contrast weightings from a single map of quantitative T1-relaxation times (qT1). This study investigated which mathematical transformations of qT1 maps, including an approximation for pseudo-proton spin density (pPSD), are best suited to derive optimized synthetic MRI contrasts for accurate SN analysis. By evaluating six dedicated qT1-derived contrast weightings in healthy subjects, this work demonstrates that a nonlinear, signal-increased pPSD-based synthetic MRI contrast (si 4 _PSD) yields a favorable balance by significantly enhancing optical contrast while maintaining a sufficient signal-to-noise ratio and preserving contrast-to-noise ratio. The si 4 _PSD images enabled highly consistent, automated atlas-based segmentation of the SN that significantly outperformed traditional manual delineation, overcoming rater variability and bias from age-dependent contrast changes. Automated segmentation revealed significant sex- and hemisphere-dependent differences in SN volume, whereas qT1 data simultaneously uncovered distinct subregional and asymmetric intrastructural aging patterns. These findings highlight that macrostructural volume and intrastructural tissue properties must be assessed as independent variables. In conclusion, this qT1-based, automated framework offers a highly consistent, scalable approach to SN mapping without extending patient scan times. By clearly separating physiological intrastructural changes affecting MRI contrasts from mistakenly perceived general atrophy, this methodology provides a powerful foundation for developing more precise and objective imaging biomarkers for SN-related neurodegenerative diseases in both research and clinical settings.

title: Whole-Brain 4D MRA With Improved Vessel Delineation Using Undersampled Multiple Overlapping Thin-Slab Radial Acquisition.
abstract: Time-resolved arterial spin labeling (ASL)-based noncontrast 4D MRA enables visualization of cerebral arterial flow dynamic patterns and holds great potential for evaluating cerebrovascular disease. However, conventional ASL 4D MRA implementations using look-locker acquisitions are susceptible to progressive RF saturation during extended readouts, leading to substantial ASL signal attenuation and loss of vessel delineation in distal arteries. These limitations potentially hinder a wider clinical translation of 4D MRA, especially when assessment of whole-brain vascular anatomy and flow dynamics is needed. This study introduces a practical and reliable ASL 4D MRA technique for whole-brain or large volumetric imaging by integrating pulsed ASL with undersampled multiple overlapping thin-slab stack-of-stars (SOS) golden-angle radial acquisition. The proposed method was evaluated against conventional single-slab 4D MRA, 3D time-of-flight magnetic resonance angiography (TOF-MRA), and pseudocontinuous ASL (pCASL)-based 4D MRA in terms of vessel delineation, blood flow dynamics, and image quality. Compared to the other methods, the proposed method substantially reduced RF saturation effects and preserved signal intensities in distal small arteries, resulting in significantly improved vessel continuity and contrast throughout the cerebral vasculature, as well as reliably capturing complete inflow-to-outflow arterial flow dynamics with good scan efficiency and image quality. The proposed technique enables high-quality, time-resolved whole-brain angiography, offering a promising noncontrast imaging tool for comprehensive assessment of cerebral arterial hemodynamics in clinical and research applications.

title: Automated Cerebrospinal Fluid Flow Quantification in Hydrocephalus Using Phase-Contrast Magnetic Resonance Imaging.
abstract: Quantitative cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) flow analysis with phase-contrast magnetic resonance imaging depends on segmentation and is affected by operator variability. This cohort method-comparison study evaluated whether a flow-aware deep learning (DL) model provides reproducible C2-C3 CSF segmentation and flow quantification compared with repeated manual segmentation. Ten hydrocephalus patients underwent 3-T phase-contrast magnetic resonance imaging at C2-C3, with 32 magnitude and phase frames across the cardiac cycle. Three experts and one novice segmented each case twice using semi-automatic software, generating 80 manual annotations. A pretrained flow-aware 2D-UNet generated one fixed automatic segmentation per case. The inference pipeline was deterministic, meaning that repeated processing of the same input with fixed model weights and settings produced identical masks. A multi-expert reference was defined as the arithmetic mean of the expert measurements. Region of interest (ROI) surface area, peak flow amplitude, and stroke volume were compared using mean difference, Bland-Altman 95% limits of agreement, Lin's concordance correlation coefficient (CCC), and intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). Expert ICC(1,1) was 0.88-0.97 for surface area, 0.97-1.00 for peak flow amplitude, and 0.97-0.99 for stroke volume; novice values were 0.63, 0.95, and 0.92, respectively. Compared with the multi-expert reference, model mean differences were -0.42 mm 2 for surface area, -0.00 mL/s for peak flow amplitude, and -0.01 mL for stroke volume, with CCC values of 0.50, 0.87, and 0.86. Bland-Altman limits of agreement were -69.12 to 68.27 mm 2 , -1.47 to 1.46 mL/s, and -0.34 to 0.31 mL. The model provided rapid, deterministic CSF segmentation with small cohort-level mean differences in peak flow amplitude and stroke volume; however, individual-level agreement with the flow-derived multi-expert reference was lower than for expert and novice segmentations obtained using the semi-automatic workflow.

title: Mapping the Evidence on Midline Catheter Tip Location, Confirmation Methods and Associated Characteristics: A Scoping Review.
abstract: Background Midline catheters (MCs) are increasingly utilized as an alternative to peripheral and central venous catheters. However, the lack of standardized protocols for tip location and confirmation methods remains a significant barrier to patient safety and clinical decision-making. Aim This scoping review aimed to systematically map the current evidence and evolving clinical practices regarding MC tip placement, specifically exploring tip location standards, confirmation methods and associated clinical characteristics. Design Scoping review. Review methods The scoping review was conducted following the Arksey and O'Malley framework and PRISMA-ScR reporting guidelines. Two independent reviewers conducted screening and data extraction, with descriptive methods used for synthesis. Data sources Eleven databases (platforms) were searched from inception to 31 August 2026: the Cochrane Library, PubMed, EMBASE, Web of Science, Scopus, ProQuest, CINAHL, CNKI, Wanfang Data, SinoMed and VIP databases. Results Out of 762 initial records, 41 publications met eligibility criteria. North American guidelines strictly restrict MC tips to the peripheral axilla, whereas European consensus advocates for deeper placement into the thoracic axillary or subclavian veins. Tip confirmation practices are heterogeneous. Methods range from external anatomical measurement to ultrasound guidance and post-procedural radiography. A significant limitation identified is the reduced reliability of ultrasound for tip visualization in patients with morbid obesity, often necessitating alternative confirmation or resulting in indeterminate placement. The quality and comparability of outcome data across studies were limited by inconsistent tip location definitions, heterogeneous patient populations and variable follow-up durations. Conclusion This review highlights substantial heterogeneity in clinical practice and guideline recommendations. The association between tip position and catheter-related complications is multifactorial. This scoping review identifies that current evidence is inadequate to support a clear preference for any single midline catheter tip-positioning strategy. These findings set an agenda for future research to inform standardized, evidence-based midline catheter practice guidelines. Implications for the profession Clinical nurses and vascular access specialists should be aware of divergent international guideline suggestions for midline catheter tip positioning. Consensus-based definitions for implantation depth and target veins, together with consistent anatomical terminology, are needed to support cross-study comparison. Optimized multimodal tip-confirmation workflows may reduce unnecessary X-ray use and improve safety, supported by targeted education and interprofessional collaboration. Future prospective cohort studies and comparative trials are needed to evaluate the relationship between tip location, confirmation strategies and patient-important clinical outcomes. Impact This scoping review synthesizes existing international literature on midline catheter tip-related practices and exposes inconsistencies across guideline documents. It draws attention to key unresolved clinical questions and provides clear directions for subsequent primary research. The findings may support the development of future consensus statements and help reduce practice variation in midline catheter care. Reporting method PRISMA-ScR. title: Using Artificial Intelligence to Identify Oropharyngeal Cancer During Fiberoptic Endoscopy.
abstract: Objective Oropharyngeal tumors with a propensity for submucosal spread can be difficult to detect and delineate during endoscopy. To facilitate their detection, we developed an Artificial Intelligence (AI) algorithm to segment tumors and other anatomically significant structures within the oropharynx. Study design Model development and validation study. Setting Tertiary academic medical center. Methods We collected videos from 106 patients undergoing pharyngolaryngoscopy, extracted 942 images, and annotated each pixel as one of 12 classes, such as tumor, uvula, and healthy mucosa. We trained an AI algorithm and evaluated its performance in multiclass and tumor-based segmentation. Results The AI algorithm achieved a recall statistic of 0.93 and a Dice score of 0.79 for tumor detection. High Dice scores were observed for pharyngeal mucosa (0.90), epiglottis (0.88), and vocal cords (0.82). Conclusions This study demonstrates that AI can semantically segment all the structures visualized during endoscopy, paving the way for computer-assisted systems for tumor identification and computer-assisted navigation during endoscopy or intubation.

title: Clinically suspected central nervous system Richter transformation presenting with progressive psychiatric symptoms: A case report.
abstract: Background Central nervous system (CNS) involvement associated with Richter transformation (RT) is a rare complication of chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL). Neurological manifestations are heterogeneous. To our knowledge, no previous reports have described CNS RT presenting predominantly with psychiatric and behavioral symptoms. We report a clinically suspected case of CNS RT presenting predominantly with progressive psychiatric symptoms in the presence of extensive CNS lesions but without apparent focal neurological deficits. Case presentation A 71-year-old man with no psychiatric history developed progressive personality change, irritability, emotional lability, behavioral disinhibition, and sleep-wake cycle disturbance. Gadolinium-enhanced fluid-attenuated inversion recovery magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated newly developed multifocal lesions predominantly involving the bilateral temporal lobes. Hematological evaluation established previously unrecognized CLL. Although histopathological confirmation was not obtained, the overall clinical, radiological, and laboratory findings supported CNS involvement associated with clinically suspected RT as the most likely diagnosis. Progressive neuropsychiatric deterioration limited invasive diagnostic procedures and disease-directed treatment. Supportive and palliative management was provided, and the patient died of aspiration pneumonia 114 days after surgery. Conclusion This case demonstrates that clinically suspected CNS RT may present predominantly with progressive psychiatric and behavioral symptoms in the absence of focal neurological deficits. Severe neuropsychiatric symptoms may themselves impede diagnostic confirmation and disease-directed treatment. When pathological confirmation is not feasible, multidisciplinary discussion and shared decision-making with the patient and family, together with explicit acknowledgment of diagnostic uncertainty and careful balancing of the benefits and burdens of further investigation and treatment, may support patient-centered care.

title: Integrated Molecular Autopsy in a Highly Consanguineous Perinatal Cohort With Severe Malformations and Strong Genetic Susceptibility.
abstract: Objective To evaluate the diagnostic yield of integrated molecular autopsy (IMA) by combining deep post-mortem phenotyping with exome (ES) and targeted genome sequencing (GS) for prenatally detected anomalies. Method This retrospective study evaluated 28 perinatal cases (22 fetuses, six neonates) with severe anomalies, normal first-tier genetics, and high consanguinity (42.9%). Deep phenotyping (radiography, macroscopy, histopathology) guided singleton ES (n = 28), supplemented by GS (n = 14) for exome-negative rescue or technical validation, and trio Sanger confirmation. The inter-method agreement between morphological hypotheses and molecular diagnoses was assessed using Cohen's Kappa. Results The IMA established a molecular diagnosis in 19 of 28 cases (67.9% yield), with system-specific yields of 100% in skeletal dysplasias (5/5), 62.5% in central nervous system defects (5/8), and 60% in cardiovascular malformations (3/5). Autosomal recessive inheritance accounted for 52.6% (10/19) of solved cases. The inter-method agreement was substantial (Cohen's Kappa = 0.81, p < 0.001). Phenotypic expansions occurred in six cases (21.4%), while nine cases (32.1%) remained unexplained. Conclusion The IMA framework achieved a high diagnostic yield of 67.9% within a highly selected, consanguineous cohort. Although clinical yield and concordance are influenced by selection biases, comprehensive post-mortem phenotyping remains essential to resolve atypical presentations, guide variant prioritization, and optimize reproductive counseling.

title: Cell Free DNA Whole Genome in Clinical Practice: A Single Center Seven-Year Experience.
abstract: Objective Cell-free DNA whole-genome screening (cfDNA-WG) is offered at our institution to patients with abnormal fetal ultrasound findings who decline diagnostic testing. We describe the cfDNA-WG performance in this clinical population. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study of singleton pregnancies with abnormal fetal ultrasound findings between April 2018 and July 2024. Descriptive data were abstracted via chart review. When diagnostic testing was performed, this was compared to the cfDNA-WG results. Results 376 subjects met the inclusion criteria. Ultrasound findings included multiple congenital anomalies (n = 123), isolated structural anomaly (n = 132), isolated soft marker (n = 63), thickened nuchal translucency (n = 50), and fetal growth restriction (n = 8). cfDNA-WG was abnormal in 24 cases (6.4%). Most abnormal results (87.5%) were common whole-chromosome aneuploidies: Trisomy 21 (n = 10), Trisomy 18 (n = 6), Trisomy 13 (n = 2), and Monosomy X (n = 3). Other abnormal results included one rare autosomal trisomy (Trisomy 22) and two copy number variants. Diagnostic testing was performed in 42 subjects (11.2%), with seven discordant results, including trisomy 8, four single-gene disorders, and two chromosomal mosaicisms. Conclusions In this cohort with abnormal ultrasound findings, abnormal cfDNA-WG results primarily reflected common aneuploidies detectable by standard cfDNA. There were five cases with normal cfDNA-WG in fetuses with significant genetic disorders, limiting the value of normal results.

title: Genetic Investigation of Pregnancies With an Isolated Fetal Pelvic Kidney.
abstract: Objective To explore genetic investigative results in fetuses with isolated pelvic kidney. Methods This was a retrospective study of 212 fetuses with isolated pelvic kidney diagnosed on second trimester anatomy ultrasound. All cases underwent invasive prenatal diagnosis for copy number variant (CNV) detection by chromosomal microarray analysis (CMA). For those with a negative CNV, trio exome sequencing (ES) was an option. Clinical and laboratory data were collected and reviewed for these cases, including maternal demographics, prenatal sonographic findings, molecular testing results, and pregnancy outcomes. Results In total, 212 cases underwent CMA testing, which identified one case of pathogenic CNV, specifically a de novo 16p11.2 microdeletion. Among the cases that yielded negative results from CMA, 118 proceeded to trio ES. Five (4.2%; 5/118) disease-causing variants across five unrelated fetuses, involving four genes: DLL1, KMT2D, PTEN and PRKG1, with two cases harboring distinct pathogenic variants in KMT2D. Following rigorous phenotype-genotype correlation assessment, only the two KMT2D variants were deemed clinically attributable, resulting in an attributable diagnostic yield of 1.7% (2/118). The remaining three variants were classified as incidental findings. With the exception of the PRKG1 variant, which was inherited from the mother, the remaining four variants were confirmed as de novo. Conclusion Our results should raise clinical awareness among obstetricians and maternal-fetal medicine specialists regarding the potential syndromic associations of pelvic kidney.

title: Results from the VANISH study: A prospective multicenter study validating a single-nucleotide polymorphism-based noninvasive prenatal test to assess aneuploidy risk in surviving twins of vanishing twin pregnancies.
abstract: To develop and validate a single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP)-based noninvasive prenatal cell-free DNA (cfDNA) screening algorithm capable of identifying the cfDNA signal of the living fetus in vanishing twin (VT) pregnancies and assessing that twin's aneuploidy risk. Prospective study enrolling participants ≥18 years old at ≥9 weeks' gestation with an ultrasound-confirmed VT at 21 US sites (August 2021 to August 2023). The study protocol specified SNP-based cfDNA screening at enrollment and at two additional 3-week intervals. Neonatal buccal swabs evaluated the SNP profile of the living fetus. Cases lost to follow-up and with missing samples were excluded. Using SNP-based technology, an algorithm to identify the living fetus was developed based on the number of fetoplacental cfDNA signals and individual fetal fraction measurements. Concordance between cfDNA in maternal plasma and newborn buccal-swab SNP profiles was used to validate the algorithm in correctly identifying the living fetus. Common aneuploidies and fetal sex were determined for the living fetus. Of 136 participants enrolled, 106 met criteria for the final analysis; 45 for development and 61 for validation. In the validation cohort, median gestational age was 10.7 weeks (range: 8.0-16.1 weeks) at ultrasound diagnosis of a VT. In 93.4% of validation cases, the algorithm identified the living fetus and gave an aneuploidy result; 90.2% within the first two blood draws. At the time the living fetus was identified, 39 samples had two fetoplacental signals and 18 had one. Aneuploidy results included 56 low-risk and one high-risk result for trisomy 21. Neonatal buccal swabs confirmed that the VT algorithm correctly identified the living twin and gave a correct aneuploidy result in 57/57 cases (100%; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 93.5%, 100.0%). Among 29 participants with all three blood draws and two fetoplacental signals at enrollment, two signals persisted in 93.1% at the second blood draw and 72.4% at the third. The SNP-based algorithm accurately identified the living fetus in VT pregnancies in this small study. Aneuploidy risk assessment was validated in all cases where the cfDNA signal for the living twin was identified, though these findings should be interpreted with caution given the limited sample size. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05004337.

title: Top-Down CSF Peptidomics Reveals Disease-Associated Peptide Signatures and Oxidative Modifications in Multiple Sclerosis and Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder.
abstract: Multiple sclerosis and neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD) are inflammatory demyelinating diseases of the CNS whose diagnosis is mainly based on clinical evidence, magnetic resonance imaging, and the analysis of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). Current approaches provide only partial insight into disease-related biological processes, thus the need for deeper characterization of CNS-derived molecular signatures has emerged. Here, we applied a high-resolution top-down peptidomic approach in CSF from treatment naïve patients with CIS, relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS), NMOSD, and non-inflammatory neurological controls. The goal was to characterize their CSF endopeptidome, unravel insights into disease-associated proteolytic remodeling and molecular signatures not accessible through conventional proteomic approaches. 381 endogenous peptides were identified, including a substantial proportion of previously unreported sequences and oxidative PTMs. Quantitative analyses revealed disease-associated alteration of the CSF endopeptidome. A newly characterized C-terminal peptide derived from secretogranin-5 progressively decreased from CIS to RRMS and represented the most informative feature for discriminating patients using random forest (RF) analysis. In contrast, NMOSD patients exhibited a distinct profile characterized by widespread peptide reduction and decreased level of oxidation. Overall, these findings support the CSF endopeptidome as a biologically informative molecular layer associated with secretory pathway alteration, PTMs, and intrathecal inflammation. SIGNIFICANCE OF THE STUDY: Top-down peptidomics directly captures endogenous peptides and their native PTMs, providing information on proteolytic processing, that is lost in conventional digestion-based workflows or immune-based targeted approaches. In this top-down exploratory study, we characterized for the first time the CSF endopeptidome of treatment-naïve patients with CIS, RRMS stratified by oligoclonal-band (OCBs) status, NMOSD, and non-inflammatory neurological controls. The results revealed disease-associated patterns of granin-, osteopontin-, proSAAS-, and fibrinogen-derived peptides, especially for oxidative derivatives. A newly characterized C-terminal secretogranin-5 peptide showed a progressive cross-sectional decrease across the CIS and RRMS groups and contributed strongly to group classification, whereas NMOSD was characterized by widespread peptide depletion and a lower representation of oxidized peptide species. These findings support the CSF endopeptidome as a complementary molecular layer for investigating regulated proteolysis and redox-dependent alteration in inflammatory demyelinating disorders and identify peptide candidates for future validation in independent cohorts.

title: Congenital Lung Malformations in Neonates: A 9-Year Tunisian Cohort Highlighting Diagnostic Challenges and Outcomes in a Resource-Limited Setting.
abstract: Background Congenital lung malformations (CLMs) represent a broad spectrum of developmental anomalies with highly variable prenatal and postnatal presentations and outcomes. Their postnatal management remains non-standardized. This study aimed to describe the spectrum of bronchopulmonary malformations diagnosed in the neonatal period, assess the contribution of antenatal and postnatal imaging, and characterize their clinical course and management in a resource-limited setting. Methods We conducted a retrospective descriptive study in the Intensive Care Unit of the Maternity and Neonatology Centre of Tunis, over a 9-year period. All newborns diagnosed with CLMs were included. Data were collected from obstetric, neonatal, and pediatric surgery records. Results Twenty-three newborns were included (prevalence: 0.23 per 1000 live births; M/F ratio: 0.91). The mean gestational age was 37.5 ± 2.9 weeks, and mean birth weight 2901 ± 833 g. Antenatal diagnosis was achieved in 65% of cases ( n=15/23 ) at a mean gestational age of 24.4 ± 4.5 weeks, following documented prenatal ultrasound screening in 74% of cases ( n=17/23 ). Respiratory distress occurred in 78% of newborns. The most frequent diagnoses were congenital pulmonary airway malformation (57%), pulmonary sequestration (22%), pulmonary hypoplasia (13%), and tracheal atresia (9%). Conservative management was used in 65% of cases, while surgery was required in four cases. In-hospital mortality was 34.8% and was significantly associated with respiratory distress (p = 0.04), delivery room resuscitation, comorbidities (p = 0.03), and associated malformations (p = 0.03). Conclusions While symptomatic CLMs in resource-limited settings carry significant early mortality due to system-level constraints, active conservative surveillance was associated with favorable outcomes in selected asymptomatic patients in this cohort when supported by structured parental education.

title: Intramuscular Fat Infiltration and Knee Osteoarthritis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Background Intramuscular fat infiltration (IMFI) is considered to be closely associated with knee osteoarthritis (KOA); however, its overall association, muscle-specific involvement, and clinical relevance remain unclear. Objective To quantify the association between IMFI and KOA, identify affected muscle groups, and evaluate prognostic value. Methods We searched PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and Embase up to December 2025 for observational studies. Two reviewers independently screened, extracted data, and assessed bias (NOS/JBI). Pooled standardized mean differences (SMDs) were calculated using random-effects models, with subgroup and sensitivity analyses. Results Seventeen studies were included. IMFI was significantly higher in KOA patients than controls (SMD = 0.63, 95% CI 0.41-0.85, I 2 = 84.7%). Anatomically, the anterior thigh muscles (rectus femoris, vastus lateralis, vastus medialis) demonstrated a significant pooled effect (SMD = 0.96, 95% CI 0.66-1.25, I 2 = 3.2%) and showed the strongest pooled association, whereas posterior, medial, and composite measures did not demonstrate significant associations. At the individual muscle level, a single study reported a notable association for the semimembranosus (SMD = 1.25, 95% CI 0.57-1.93); however, this finding is based on limited evidence and requires confirmation in future studies. Subgroup by imaging modality: CT demonstrated a significant association (SMD = 0.59, 95% CI 0.28-0.90), while MRI and ultrasound did not show significant associations. Elevated IMFI was also associated with reduced muscle strength, higher KOA incidence, structural progression, and increased knee replacement risk. Conclusion A moderate positive association exists between IMFI and KOA, with notable muscle-specific heterogeneity. Anterior thigh muscles show the strongest pooled association, whereas individual muscle findings require further confirmation. These findings suggest that IMFI may represent a promising potential marker warranting further prospective investigation for risk stratification, though causality and its role in modifying disease progression remain to be established.

title: Evaluation of Concordance between Radiation Therapists and Medical Physicists in MR-Guided Online Adaptive Planning.
abstract: Purpose Magnetic resonance (MR) -guided online adaptive radiotherapy requires skill in online adaptive treatment planning. The aim of this study was to demonstrate that radiation therapists, with appropriate training, can consistently produce high-quality adaptive plans concordant with those created by medical physicists for treatment on a 1.5 Tesla MR-Linac (MRL). Methods We evaluated plans generated by two experienced MRL radiation therapists and two MR-Linac medical physicists using an adapt-to-position (ATP) workflow to treat 10 patients with head and neck cancer; this workflow includes an iso-center shift and plan re-optimization to account for setup discrepancy between simulation and treatment. For each adaptive session, CT-MR images were fused and isocenter translational shifts recorded. Differences among the three roles (Therapist, Physicist 1, Physicist 2) were assessed by repeated-measures analysis of variance (RM-ANOVA) and Bonferroni-corrected post-hoc paired t tests, reported as secondary, exploratory analyses. Agreement on shifts and dosimetric endpoints was quantified with Lin's concordance correlation coefficient (CCC), with bias-corrected and accelerated bootstrap 95% confidence intervals (CIs), as the primary analysis. Results No significant differences were observed among roles for X- or Y-axis shifts ( p = 0.804 and p = 0.950). A statistically significant difference was observed for Z-axis shifts ( p = 0.005), driven by Therapist versus Physicist 1 (Bonferroni-adjusted p = 0.015; mean paired difference 0.10 cm, 95% CI 0.04-0.17 cm), a systematic difference of approximately 1 mm that is small relative to clinical planning margins. CCC point estimates were 0.866-0.970 for translational shifts and 0.972-0.997 for target coverage and maximum dose, with no point estimate in the poor-agreement range (CCC < 0.80). Bootstrap 95% CIs were wide for the shifts, as expected at n = 10, but therapist-physicist agreement was comparable to physicist-physicist agreement for every endpoint, and CI lower bounds for the dosimetric endpoints were ≥0.75 (maximum dose ≥0.97). Conclusion Our results showed good concordance between adaptive plans created by radiation therapists and medical physicists in the ATP workflow for head and neck cancer, suggesting that appropriately trained therapists can produce high-quality adaptive plans in this specific context. These conclusions are limited to the ATP workflow and to head and neck cancer; extension to other sites or to the adapt-to-shape (ATS) workflow requires independent investigation.

title: Exploratory Analysis of Peri-Prostatic Adipose Tissue Radiomics Features and Their Potential to Predict Prostate Cancer Diagnosis: Results From a UK Biobank Study.
abstract: Introduction This paper reports the development and application of an artificial intelligence (AI)-led approach to large volume MRI data curation and image segmentation of periprostatic adipose tissue (PPAT) in prostate cancer (PCa)-free men from the UK Biobank. We report how PPAT was defined, radiomics features of PPAT extracted, and explored their potential to predict a PCa diagnosis. Methodology In total, MR images from 31,042 non-PCa men were extracted and made available for autosegmentation. PPAT was defined using tools in 3D Slicer as anterior (Ant PPAT) or posterior (Post PPAT) in relation to Denonvilliers fascia. Dice-Sørensen coefficients (DICE) were calculated to measure the agreement between the observer's manual segmentations used to train a 3D convolutional neural network with U-Net architecture (nnU-Net). Radiomics features were extracted using PyRadiomics and logistic regression analysis was performed on the Ant and Post PPAT features that were deemed significantly different between men without PCa and those who went on to develop PCa. Statistical analysis was performed in SPSS (version 29.0.0). Results A total of 107 features (14 shape, 18 first-order texture and 75 second-order texture) were extracted from auto-segmentations of Ant PPAT and Post PPAT. A case-control radiomics analysis was performed on 297 men who had an MRI scan when cancer-free (but who subsequently went on to be diagnosed with PCa), age-matched (within 1 year) to participants without a PCa diagnosis during the follow-up period. In Ant PPAT there were statistically significant differences in 31 features compared to 4 in Post PPAT between men without PCa and those with prevalent PCa. Stratifying the data by the prevalent PCa group time to diagnosis had a limited effect on these results. Predictive analysis results were not statistically significant for Ant PPAT or Post PPAT, however are comparable with the reported predictive value of other clinically established biomarkers of PCa. Conclusion An automated process for data curation and image segmentation was successfully demonstrated. Results suggest that Ant PPAT justifies further investigation as a predictive biomarker for prostate cancer diagnosis.

title: 4D-Flow MRI-Derived Wall Shear Stress as a Non-Invasive Biomarker for the Detection and Hemodynamic Characterization of Pulmonary Hypertension.
abstract: Invasive right heart catheterization (RHC) remains the reference standard for diagnosing pulmonary hypertension (PH), but there is a pressing need for non-invasive techniques to assess pulmonary hemodynamics. This study evaluates 4D-flow MRI-derived wall shear stress (WSS) for PH detection using the updated 2022 hemodynamic criteria, and the prediction of right ventriculo-pulmonary arterial (RV-PA) uncoupling to assess disease severity. 3D WSS was measured in the main (MPA), right (RPA), and left (LPA) pulmonary arteries in a retrospective validation cohort (41 PH patients, 23 non-PH) and then assessed in a prospective test cohort (23 PH patients, 17 healthy controls). For methodological validation, a patient-specific computational fluid dynamics (CFD) was performed in a subset of 16 patients from the validation cohort. RV-PA uncoupling was assessed on the cine MRI, using RV global longitudinal strain (GLS) < -15.3% and RVSV/RVESV < 1. Both 3D peak and time-averaged WSS were significantly reduced in PH patients compared with healthy controls. Global WSS metrics demonstrated the strongest correlations with invasive hemodynamic parameters, including mPAP ( r = -0.75, p < 0.001) and PVR ( r = -0.76, p < 0.001). ROC curve analysis identified a peak WSS cutoff of < 0.30 Pa (AUC 0.98) for PH detection, a threshold achieving 90% sensitivity and 100% specificity in the test cohort. Furthermore, a peak WSS threshold of < 0.18 Pa demonstrated excellent discriminative ability for RV-PA uncoupling. These findings support the potential integration of WSS analysis into routine CMR protocols as a non-invasive complement to RHC, showing promise for both diagnosis and a longitudinal biomarker for monitoring PH.

title: Giant Intrapulmonary Solitary Fibrous Tumour With a Possible Liver Metastasis: A Rare Case.
abstract: Intrapulmonary solitary fibrous tumours (SFTs) are exceptionally rare mesenchymal neoplasms, particularly when presenting as giant thoracic masses. We report a case of a 57-year-old woman with progressive chest pain and dyspnoea who initially presented with pleural effusion and hypoglycaemia and received empirical anti-tuberculosis therapy without improvement. Contrast-enhanced CT revealed a left lower lobe mass enlarging to 11 × 16.5 × 15.2 cm on repeat imaging, with rightward cardiac displacement, pericardial effusion and a hepatic nodule suspicious for metastasis to the liver. Core needle biopsy revealed a low-grade spindle cell neoplasm. Immunohistochemistry revealed diffuse STAT6 positivity, partial CD34 positivity, Ki-67 < 5%, and negativity for CK7, desmin, SMA and S100, supporting the diagnosis of SFT. Following a multidisciplinary evaluation, six cycles of systemic chemotherapy were administered, and the patient remained clinically stable. This case highlights the diagnostic challenges of giant intrapulmonary SFT and the pivotal role of STAT6 immunohistochemistry in establishing the diagnosis.

title: The Bird's Nest Sign as an Initial Presentation of Primary Pulmonary B-Cell Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma With Plasmacytic Differentiation.
abstract: The bird's nest sign (BNS) has been described as a sign on chest computed tomography (CT) in various pulmonary diseases. We report a rare case of primary pulmonary B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma with plasmacytic differentiation presenting with BNS, mimicking an invasive fungal disease at first. A 61-year-old Vietnamese man with a history of idiopathic thrombocytopenia and splenectomy 3 years prior to admission presented with prolonged dry cough, mild dyspnoea on exertion and chest discomfort for 3 weeks. His laboratory tests were unremarkable, but his chest CT showed bilateral consolidation with the BNS. After an unfavourable response to anti-fungal therapy, the second transthoracic lung biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of primary pulmonary B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma with plasmacytic differentiation. This case highlights the importance of considering lymphoma in the differential diagnosis of BNS when infection is excluded and concurrently seeking a confirmatory diagnosis with repeated diagnostic procedures when necessary.

A 61-year-old Vietnamese man with a history of idiopathic thrombocytopenia and splenectomy 3 years prior to admission presented with prolonged dry cough, mild dyspnoea on exertion and chest discomfort for 3 weeks. title: Discordant Cavitary Changes: A Radiological Dilemma in Invasive Mucinous Adenocarcinoma: A Case Report.
abstract: Treatment-related cavitary transformation in lung cancer may complicate radiological response assessment. We report a man in his 70s with stage IVA invasive mucinous adenocarcinoma treated with atezolizumab, bevacizumab, carboplatin and paclitaxel. After two cycles, CT showed enlargement of cavitary components despite regression of solid tumour components, making response assessment difficult. After two additional cycles, the pulmonary lesions showed little change, whereas progression of the Th4 bone metastasis led to an overall assessment of progressive disease and a change to docetaxel plus ramucirumab. Thereafter, the cavities further enlarged while the cavity walls progressively thinned and the solid components appeared to regress. This case illustrates that marked multifocal cavitary transformation may produce discordant morphological changes, limiting response assessment based on imaging alone. Serum CEA and SLX levels remained within the normal ranges at diagnosis and throughout treatment.

title: Predictive Model for Identifying Fibrotic Interstitial Lung Abnormalities on Computed Tomography for Respiratory Specialists.
abstract: Background and objective Interstitial lung abnormalities (ILAs) are often unreported, and fibrotic ILAs carry a worse prognosis. In this study, we aimed to develop and validate a prediction model for fibrotic ILAs using non-radiological factors. Methods Using data from the Kumamoto ILA study (a multicenter prospective cohort in Japan), we developed a four-variable model (age, pack-years, fine crackles, elevated serum surfactant protein-D) in 164 patients (2022-2023, derivation cohort) and temporally validated it in 207 patients (2023-2024, validation cohort), with internal-external cross-validation for between-center heterogeneity. A simplified integer score was similarly assessed against 24-month functional decline and treatment initiation within 3 years. Results Fibrotic ILAs comprised 82% of cases (approximately 60% subsequently met ATS-defined ILD criteria), consistent across cohorts. The four-variable model achieved an AUC of 0.79 (derivation) and 0.76 (validation; pooled 0.76, 95% CI 0.68-0.82), with good calibration and minimal between-center heterogeneity. The integer score performed similarly (AUC 0.79/0.75) and correlated with functional decline (%FVC ≥ 10% or %DLco ≥ 15%) and treatment initiation. Conclusion Age, smoking exposure, fine crackles, and elevated serum surfactant protein-D are key predictors of progressive fibrotic ILAs, supporting early risk stratification and clinical decision-making. Trial registration UMIN000045149/2021.12.1.

title: 3D Reconstruction of Nanoparticle Distribution in Tumor Spheroids With Volume Electron Microscopy.
abstract: Spatially resolved characterization of nanomaterial (NM) distribution within cellular ultrastructure is essential for understanding NM fate and activity in biological systems. Volume electron microscopy (vEM) is uniquely positioned to address this challenge, yet fully documented quantitative pipelines that simultaneously segment NMs and cellular structures remain scarce. Here, an end-to-end analytical pipeline is presented based on the example of serial block-face scanning electron microscopy (SBF-SEM) data of tumor spheroids containing nanoparticles (NPs). A hybrid segmentation strategy is adopted, comprising a fine-tuned Cellpose-SAM model for cells and nuclei, and an empirical Bayes approach for AuNPs. The fine-tuned model outperforms both the pre-trained baseline and the benchmark experiments in Amira, and shows good generalization to 2D EM datasets of varying sample types, suggesting potential as a general-purpose segmentation model for electron microscopy. Full 3D reconstruction of NP distributions reveals preferential clustering in the perinuclear region, with a median nucleus-to-NP distance of 2.57 μm and NM uptake spanning several orders of magnitude across cells. Furthermore, morphological analysis of segmented cells and nuclei using 3D shape descriptors and local curvature metrics provides quantitative access to features inaccessible from single sections. Together, these results establish a reproducible, open framework for the joint quantitative analysis of NM distribution and cellular morphology in vEM data.

title: Functional Nucleic Acid-Antibody Conjugates for Effective Tumor Targeted Therapy With Controllable Side Effects.
abstract: Antibody-guided therapeutics, including antibody-drug conjugates and radiopharmaceuticals, efficiently deliver payloads to tumor lesions, but the weeks-long half-life of antibodies promotes accumulation in normal tissues, increasing the risk of off-target toxicity. Although conventional linkers generally provide systemic stability, recent studies indicate that retention of intact antibody-guided conjugates in normal tissues can cause chronic toxicity. Here, we report an antibody-guided delivery platform leveraging the pH-responsive properties of i-motif functional nucleic acids (iM) for targeted chemo- and radiotherapy. Using trastuzumab as the targeting moiety, the platform (Tra-iM) achieves selective payload delivery. Within the acidic tumor microenvironment, the i-motif forms a stable quadruplex, promoting effective payload accumulation in tumor lesions. Under physiological conditions, nuclease-sensitive linear i-motif structures trigger rapid disassembly of Tra-iM, generating hydrophilic nucleic acid fragments that minimize off-target penetration and facilitate clearance of hydrophobic payloads. Fluorescence and PET imaging showed reduced normal-organ retention and faster clearance of the labeled payload-bearing components. Therapeutic evaluations demonstrate that Tra-iM preserves targeted delivery and efficacy while markedly reducing hematologic and hepatic toxicity after high-dose administration. This strategy significantly enhances the biosafety of antibody-guided therapeutics and highlights the potential of metabolite-regulated delivery platforms to advance targeted nanomedicine.

title: Recent Advances in Wearable Ultrasound Patches for Healthcare Applications.
abstract: Wearable ultrasound patches, as a transformative innovation redefining the boundaries of traditional ultrasound medicine, signify a shift from hospital-centered, episodic diagnosis and therapy toward portable, personalized, and continuous healthcare solutions. As an emerging and rapidly evolving research direction, fully integrated wearable ultrasound platforms-synergistically combining real-time imaging, closed-loop sensing, and on-demand therapeutic intervention within a single conformal patch and system-have been progressively utilized for chronic disease management and closed-loop neuromodulation. This review summarizes and discusses the advanced wearable ultrasound technologies to provide insight into the underlying strategies that enable the convergence of diagnosis and therapy in diverse disease scenarios. This review primarily focuses on wearable ultrasound patches and systems for cardiovascular monitoring, musculoskeletal assessment, neurological treatment, sonodynamic therapy, drug delivery, and integrated theranostics. In addition, the challenges and development prospects of wearable ultrasound patches are analyzed to promote further clinical translation, with emphasis on the synergistic optimization of imaging and therapy, long-term integration reliability, and fully integrated portable designs. It is earnestly expected that this kind of flexible-electronics-enabled wearable ultrasound technology will stimulate comprehensive investigation and promote the clinical development of next-generation multifunctional theranostic platforms.

title: Patient-Informed Biomechanical Modeling Reveals Mechanical Mechanism of Brain Damage in Idiopathic Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus.
abstract: Idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus (iNPH) is a globally growing neurological disorder in older adults that is radiologically characterized by enlargement of ventricles. However, it remains unknown whether ventricular enlargement can produce biomechanical loading large enough to drive brain morphological changes and tissue damage. Here, we develop an anatomically detailed biomechanical model of aging human brain and apply ventricular enlargement using a three-dimensional displacement field derived from MRI of iNPH patients and age-matched controls. The model accurately reproduces radiological markers of iNPH, including Evans index, callosal angle, and high-convexity sulcal narrowing. It further predicts large mechanical strains in the periventricular white matter, particularly within the corona radiata, corpus callosum, and anterior thalamic radiations, tracts consistently implicated in iNPH imaging abnormalities. These findings provide strong evidence that ventricular enlargement induces mechanical strain that contributes to iNPH brain abnormalities, which can potentially be reversed by reducing strain following shunting surgery. The biomechanical brain model forms the foundation of a predictive digital platform and future "digital twin" technology to support diagnosis, patient stratification, and treatment planning in iNPH.

title: Depth-Aware Machine Learning for 3D Reconstruction of Fibrous Porous Electrodes by FIB-SEM Tomography.
abstract: Quantitative three-dimensional reconstruction of porous polymers with sub-micrometer feature sizes is central to understanding and designing electrochemical interfaces and membranes. However, focused ion beam-scanning electron microscopy tomography combined with conventional segmentation techniques cannot readily reconstruct complex disordered morphologies such as fibers. Standard segmentation workflows misclassify out-of-plane material as in-plane material, distorting the reconstructed pore network, fiber connectivity, and interface area. Here, we introduce an annotation-free, depth-aware machine-learning framework that combines monocular depth estimation, trained on macroscale images, with unsupervised clustering to separate in-plane polymer cross-sections from subsurface contributions in serial FIB-SEM tomography images. Applied to copper-coated electrospun poly(vinylidene fluoride-co-hexafluoropropylene) fiber mats, the approach produces 3D reconstructions that preserve fibrous morphology more faithfully than conventional supervised and unsupervised segmentation. Quantitative validation against capillary flow porometry, pycnometry, and high-resolution wide-angle X-ray computed tomography demonstrates improved agreement across pore cross-section diameter, fiber volume ratio, and Cu depth decrease metrics. This work establishes depth-aware segmentation as a transferable strategy from real-scale to nanoscale imaging, requiring no labeled training data and enabling accurate 3D segmentation and reconstruction from SEM images. This approach opens a path toward more reliable structure-property relationships in disordered porous polymer materials.

title: A Metal-Free Nitroxide Radical Nanoliposome for MRI-Guided Therapy of Ulcerative Colitis.
abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) remains challenging to diagnose and treat because of the limited sensitivity of current imaging techniques, the safety concerns associated with metal-based magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) contrast agents, and the insufficient efficacy of conventional anti-inflammatory therapies. Here, we report a metal-free theranostic nanoliposome (A@Clip) that integrates nitroxide radical-containing phospholipids (TEMPO-lipids) and 5-aminosalicylic acid (5-ASA) into a biocompatible liposomal platform for MRI-guided therapy of UC. The liposomal architecture enhances the T1 MRI performance of TEMPO radicals while enabling efficient reactive oxygen species scavenging and anti-inflammatory drug delivery. A@Clip exhibits excellent biocompatibility, promotes cellular uptake, and effectively suppresses oxidative stress and inflammatory responses in vitro. In a murine colitis model, A@Clip enables sensitive visualization of inflamed colon tissue and markedly alleviates disease progression, intestinal injury, inflammatory responses, and gut microbiota dysbiosis without detectable systemic toxicity. This work establishes a metal-free nanotheranostic strategy for integrating non-invasive MRI with anti-inflammatory therapy and provides a versatile platform for the precision management of inflammatory diseases.

title: Regional growth patterns of fetal corpus callosum at 18-32 weeks' gestation assessed by three-dimensional transvaginal neurosonography.
abstract: Objectives To evaluate the normal development of the fetal corpus callosum (CC) between 18 and 32 weeks' gestation using three-dimensional (3D) transvaginal neurosonography and to assess the effect of volume contrast imaging (VCI) on the measurement of fetal CC biometry. Methods This study included two cohorts of women with a singleton pregnancy: a prospective cohort attending the research clinic at Prince of Wales Hospital in Hong Kong SAR, China, between April 2019 and February 2025, at which 3D fetal brain volumes were acquired prospectively, and a retrospective cohort attending CRIFM Prenatal Medical Clinic in Osaka, Japan, between December 2018 and March 2025, from which archived 3D fetal brain volume datasets were retrieved. In both cohorts, 3D fetal brain volume data of the CC were acquired using transvaginal neurosonography between 18 and 32 weeks' gestation using the same acquisition protocol. Inclusion criteria were appropriately grown fetuses at 18 + 0 to 32 + 6 weeks' gestation, without suspected structural or chromosomal defects. In the midsagittal plane, using 3D volume multiplanar imaging, the CC length and total area were obtained and regional thickness at the genu, body and splenium were measured following a modified Garel's method. Additionally, the areas of five vertical CC segments defined by arithmetic fractions of the CC length following Witelson's classification (anterior one-third, anterior midbody, posterior midbody, isthmus and splenium) were obtained. All fetal biometric measurements were performed using non-VCI and VCI modes. Measurements obtained using non-VCI and VCI modes were compared using the paired t-test. Generalized Additive Models for Location, Scale and Shape (GAMLSS) were used to explore the relationship between all biometric measurements of the fetal CC and gestational age. The final models were used to derive percentiles and construct reference curves. Intra- and interobserver variability were assessed using 30 randomly selected cases. Results A total of 956 fetuses at 18-32 weeks' gestation were included. Gestational age-specific trajectories of fetal CC biometry were established, demonstrating distinct, non-linear growth patterns in CC length, total area, genu, body and splenium thicknesses and the areas of five individual CC subdivisions from 18 to 32 weeks. Overall, the genu and body thicknesses increased sharply from 18 weeks to 23 weeks. Thereafter, genu thickness continued to increase gradually until 32 weeks, whereas body thickness plateaued before showing renewed growth at 31-32 weeks. The percentile curve for fetal CC total area demonstrated a steady increase from 18 to 32 weeks. Among the five subdivisions of the CC, the splenium demonstrated the most pronounced absolute area growth, reaching a median of approximately 0.40 cm 2 by 32 weeks, with markedly greater expansion than the midbody regions throughout the second to early third trimesters. Fetal CC biometric measurements were comparable between non-VCI and VCI measurements. Overall, the biometric measurements demonstrated high reproducibility, with most showing good-to-excellent intra- and interobserver reliability, except for moderate interobserver reliability for genu and body thicknesses. Conclusions We have characterized region-specific non-linear growth patterns in fetal CC development from 18 to 32 weeks, with posterior-predominant area expansion most pronounced in the splenium. The clinical significance of regional CC measurements remains uncertain, and the presented trajectories should be regarded as descriptions of normal developmental patterns rather than as reference charts for isolated clinical decision-making. Longitudinal studies incorporating postnatal neurodevelopmental assessment will be required to determine their prognostic value. © 2026 The Author(s). title: Growth trajectory and miscarriage diagnosis threshold in early IVF pregnancy: multicenter study.
abstract: Objectives To characterize early-pregnancy ultrasound findings in pregnancies conceived via in-vitro fertilization (IVF) for which gestational age is known precisely based on the date of embryo transfer (ET), and to examine their association with first-trimester pregnancy outcome. Methods This was a retrospective multicenter cohort study of fresh- and frozen-cycle IVF pregnancies from 14 centers across England between January 2022 and December 2024, with one center contributing additional data from January 2019 to December 2021. Patients with a confirmed intrauterine pregnancy at the first transvaginal ultrasound scan (≤ 9 + 6 weeks' gestation) after ET were included for analysis of pregnancy outcome. Data collected included the date of ET, embryo stage at transfer, early-pregnancy ultrasound measurements, including crown-rump length (CRL) and mean sac diameter (MSD), and expected gestational age. The endpoint was viability at the 11-14-week dating scan. CRL growth was modeled against gestational age using quadratic regression. The diagnostic performance of a range of gestational-age cut-offs for identifying miscarriage was evaluated using sensitivity, specificity and positive predictive value (PPV). Results A total of 10 009 IVF pregnancies were included, of which 8223 (82.2%) were viable at 11-14 weeks and 1786 (17.8%) were non-viable. A significant difference was found in the distribution of CRL measurements at the first ultrasound scan between pregnancies that were found to be viable and those that were non-viable at the subsequent 11-14-week scan (P < 0.001). When stratified by gestational age based on the date of ET, viable pregnancies had a higher median CRL than pregnancies of the same gestational age that subsequently ended in miscarriage, although there was a degree of overlap in the distribution of CRL values between the two groups. Furthermore, among pregnancies that were viable at 11-14 weeks, significant variability was seen in CRL and MSD measurements at each gestational age. The estimated mean CRL growth rate was 0.926 mm/day from when CRL was first measurable. The ultrasound finding of an empty gestational sac at or beyond 47 days' gestation based on the date of ET (n = 406) had a PPV of 100% and specificity of 100% (95% CI, 94.9-100%) for first-trimester miscarriage. Conclusions Early-pregnancy ultrasound measurements in IVF pregnancy show wide physiological variability at any given gestational age, even when gestational age can be calculated precisely from the date of ET. An empty gestational sac at or beyond 47 days' gestation was associated with 100% PPV and 100% specificity for non-viable pregnancy. Further external validation in independent cohorts is required to confirm this potential threshold for diagnosing miscarriage in IVF pregnancy. © 2026 The Author(s). title: Effect of ultrasound-guided visual biofeedback performed by midwives on duration of second stage of labor: randomized controlled trial.
abstract: Objective To investigate whether coached maternal pushing using transperineal ultrasound (TPUS)-guided visual biofeedback, performed by midwives, reduces the duration of the second stage of labor and affects the mode of delivery in nulliparous women receiving epidural analgesia. Methods This was a single-center randomized controlled trial of nulliparous women with a singleton term pregnancy with an estimated fetal weight of 2500-4000 g, who were in the active stage of labor and were receiving epidural analgesia, conducted between May 2021 and August 2024. Consenting participants were assigned randomly to one of two groups: the study group (sonographic-coaching group), who were coached using TPUS-guided visual biofeedback, or the control group (traditional-coaching group), who were coached using the traditional vaginal technique. Coached maternal pushing with TPUS-guided visual biofeedback included a demonstration of the direction of effective pushing by visualizing the real-time downward movement of the fetal head on a television screen in front of the woman. Coaching sessions were conducted following epidural administration during the active stage of labor and after the diagnosis of complete cervical dilatation, with an additional session conducted if delivery had not occurred within 2 h after complete cervical dilatation. Coaching was led exclusively by midwives, with no involvement of obstetricians. Outcomes were compared between the groups. Results A total of 327 women were randomized and included, comprising 168 women in the sonographic-coaching group and 159 in the traditional-coaching group. Demographic and baseline characteristics, including maternal body mass index and rates of labor induction and oxytocin use, were similar in both groups. The second stage of labor was significantly shorter in the sonographic-coaching group compared with the traditional-coaching group (mean ± SD, 107 ± 59 min vs 132 ± 71 min; P = 0.001). The sonographic-coaching group also showed lower rates of second-degree or higher perineal tears (65.4% vs 77.3%; P = 0.020) and intrapartum fever (8.9% vs 16.4%; P = 0.043). Other secondary outcomes, including neonatal birth weight and 5-min Apgar score, did not differ significantly between the groups. No significant differences were observed in the mode of delivery. Conclusions Coached maternal pushing using TPUS-guided visual biofeedback, performed by midwives, significantly reduced the duration of the second stage of labor and the incidence of second-degree or higher perineal tears and intrapartum fever. Larger studies are warranted to further assess its impact on delivery outcome. © 2026 International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology.

title: Association of quantitative vascularization of the anterior fornix/cervix region with placenta accreta spectrum and associated intraoperative hemorrhage.
abstract: Objectives We aimed to evaluate a quantitative method for analyzing vascularization in the anterior fornix/cervix (AFC) region in women at risk of placenta accreta spectrum (PAS). The primary aim was to evaluate the association between quantitative vascularization (QV) and severity of PAS (determined by histopathology) and to estimate the optimal QV cut-off value to predict PAS. A secondary aim was to evaluate the association of QV with severe intraoperative blood loss (IOBL). Methods This was a prospective study including patients with anterior placenta previa referred for suspected PAS at the University of Texas Health Science Center at Houston, TX, USA, between December 2021 and June 2025. Transvaginal ultrasound with color Doppler (with standardized settings) was performed to visualize the cervix and the lower uterine segment in the midsagittal plane. The prenatal diagnosis of high risk for PAS was based on ultrasound features including loss of the uteroplacental interface, the presence of placental lacunae, increased vascularization and abnormal bladder wall. For QV assessment, a videoclip was acquired, in which the AFC region was defined and post-processing analysis was used to estimate the percentage of color pixels within the AFC region in each frame. The mean value across all frames was defined as the QV value. QV values were not provided to clinicians and were not used for clinical decisions. Associations between QV and PAS, depth of implantation, IOBL and units of blood products transfused were evaluated, as well as the ability of QV to discriminate between patients with and those without PAS. Results A total of 117 patients were included. PAS was confirmed histopathologically in 89 (76.1%) patients (placenta accreta, n = 11; placenta increta, n = 55; placenta percreta, n = 23). A reliable estimation of IOBL was obtained in 109 patients and severe IOBL (> 1500 mL) occurred in 53 (48.6%) of these cases. The area under the receiver-operating-characteristics curve, demonstrating the ability of QV to discriminate between cases with and those without confirmed PAS, was 0.821 (95% CI, 0.739-0.886). The optimal QV cut-off value was 8.5%, yielding a sensitivity of 70.5% (95% CI, 59.8-79.7%), specificity of 89.7% (95% CI, 68.3-96.1%), positive predictive value of 93.9% (95% CI, 86.1-97.5%) and negative predictive value of 50.0% (95% CI, 40.3-57.8%). QV ≥ 8.5% was associated with increased odds of PAS (odds ratio (OR), 14.9 (95% CI, 4.7-47.0); P < 0.0001), placenta percreta (OR, 55.5 (95% CI, 10.1-305.7); P < 0.0001), severe IOBL (OR, 3.9 (95% CI, 1.8-8.7); P = 0.0009) and the need for ≥ 4 units of blood products during delivery (OR, 4.6 (95% CI, 2.0-10.4); P = 0.0002). Conclusion QV ≥ 8.5% of the AVC region identifies patients at increased risk for PAS and for severe IOBL. Although the negative predictive value was limited, QV assessment of the AFC region may provide valuable information to support clinical management and surgical planning in PAS. © 2026 International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology.

title: Diagnostic Imaging Analysis of Humerus Bone Structure in Long-Legged Buzzard (Buteo rufinus): Radiology and CT-Scan Insights.
abstract: Background Advanced imaging techniques, particularly computed tomography (CT), are revolutionising veterinary diagnostics by providing detailed structural insights essential for accurate diagnosis and treatment planning. Objectives This study aimed to compare the efficacy of CT imaging and digital radiography in the diagnosis and treatment of raptors, with the goal of identifying the more precise and efficient imaging technique for clinical management. By evaluating these methods, the research seeks to optimise diagnostic accuracy and treatment planning, ultimately improving rehabilitation outcomes for birds of prey requiring high-precision care. Methods This study evaluated the humerus bone structure of 10 adult Long-legged Buzzard (Buteo rufinus) individuals using digital radiology and CT imaging. Birds were sedated to minimise stress, and both left and right humerus structures were examined. Humerus indices, including cranio-caudal diameter, medullary cavity diameter, cortical thickness and bone density, were measured to compare the effectiveness of the two modalities. Results Results of this study revealed significant differences in humerus indices between radiology and CT techniques (P < 0.05), with CT providing more accurate and detailed measurements. CT excelled in visualising internal structures, such as the cortex and medullary cavity, offering superior diagnostic clarity. No significant differences were observed between left and right humerus indices (P > 0.05), indicating consistent bilateral symmetry. Conclusions The study concludes that CT imaging is superior to digital radiology for assessing humerus bone structure in the long-legged buzzard, providing precise information crucial for managing humeral injuries. These findings underscore the clinical utility of CT in avian veterinary medicine, particularly for raptors and recommend This technique helps surgeons prepare the necessary equipment more accurately and use more precise methods, ultimately increasing the success rate of surgeries.
