title: Partial injury of the triradiate cartilage following low-energy trauma.
abstract: Background Acute traumatic injuries of the triradiate cartilage are very rare in children and usually result from high-energy trauma associated with other pelvic injuries. Only two sports-related cases of complete injuries of the triradiate cartilage have been reported to date. Case presentation We herein describe the first case of a partial injury of the triradiate cartilage in a 14-year-old athlete. The patient presented with sudden-onset hip pain and moderate functional impairment. The fracture was confined to the ilioischial synchondrosis, while the remaining triradiate cartilage and the contralateral side were fused. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) suggested the diagnosis, which was confirmed by a computed tomography (CT) scanner. Conclusion This case highlights the importance of carefully evaluating the triradiate cartilage on imaging in young athletes with sudden-onset hip pain, even when the triradiate cartilage remains partially open unilaterally.

title: Thrombosed mycotic aneurysm of the cervical internal carotid artery mimicking a parapharyngeal abscess in a child: a case report of multimodal imaging diagnosis.
abstract: A parapharyngeal abscess, although relatively rare, is a potentially life-threatening deep neck space infection in the pediatric population that carries a risk of serious complications. Mycotic pseudoaneurysm of the cervical internal carotid artery (ICA) is a rare vascular complication in children that can lead to catastrophic hemorrhage if misdiagnosed and attempted for surgical incision. We report a 7-year-old malnourished boy presenting with fever, dysphagia, and neck stiffness. Suboptimal contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) suggested a left parapharyngeal abscess, and surgical drainage was planned. A dedicated CT, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) with diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) mapping, magnetic resonance angiography, and three-dimensional CT angiography identified a completely thrombosed mycotic pseudoaneurysm rather than an abscess. This case demonstrates that complete thrombosis transforms a mycotic pseudoaneurysm into a mass that can easily be mistaken for an abscess without the right imaging modalities and high-quality imaging.

title: Deep learning-based synthetic CT for the assessment of spinal structural lesions in axial spondyloarthritis.
abstract: Objective To evaluate the accuracy of synthetic CT for detecting spinal structural lesions in patients with suspected axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA). Materials and methods Patients with inflammatory back pain who underwent both spinal CT and MRI examinations were included in this retrospective study. Two readers independently assessed the presence of structural lesions (facet joint ankylosis, structural Andersson lesions, discal ossifications, vertebral ankylosis, syndesmophytes, and erosions) on conventional CT and synthetic CT images. Feature detection accuracy of synthetic CT relative to conventional CT was evaluated using sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, and negative predictive value, with consensus reading as the reference standard. In addition, lesion-level erosion detection accuracy was assessed, and erosion size was compared between conventional CT and synthetic CT. Results Eighty-seven patients (mean age, 41 ± 14.2 years; range, 18-80 years; 42 males and 45 females) were included. Sensitivity of synthetic CT was 1.00 for facet joint ankylosis, structural Andersson lesions, vertebral ankylosis, and erosions, 0.91 for syndesmophytes, and 0.67 for discal ossifications. Specificity ranged from 0.97 to 1.00 across all lesion types. Lesion-level analysis showed sensitivity of 0.82-1.00 and specificity of 0.96-1.00 for erosion detection across different spinal regions. No significant differences of erosion size (median [IQR], mm) between conventional CT and synthetic CT (width, 7.7 [4.4-9.7] vs. 8.0 [4.1-9.6], P = 0.15; depth, 4.5 [3.5-6.7] vs. 4.5 [3.5-6.5], P = 0.12). Conclusion Synthetic CT demonstrates a high feature detection accuracy for assessing most spinal structural lesions in patients with suspected axSpA.

title: Applications and performance of imaging artificial intelligence in detecting and staging avascular necrosis of the femoral head: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Objective To evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of imaging artificial intelligence (AI) models for detecting avascular necrosis of the femoral head (AVNFH) and to examine whether diagnostic performance differs according to imaging modality, disease-stage focus, and validation strategy. Materials and methods In accordance with PRISMA-DTA, we conducted a systematic search in four main databases. Two independent reviewers evaluated the studies, extracted relevant data, and assessed the quality following the QUADAS-2 criteria. The primary analysis pooled overall sensitivity and specificity using a bivariate random-effects model. Prespecified subgroup analyses assessed differences by imaging modality, disease stage focus, and evaluation strategy. Results Nine selected estimates contributed to the primary analysis of binary AVNFH detection. Pooled sensitivity was 0.888 (95% CI, 0.789-0.944), specificity was 0.937 (95% CI, 0.906-0.958), and SROC AUC was 0.967. MRI-based estimates showed higher sensitivity than radiography-based estimates in the study-level comparison (p = 0.027). No significant subgroup differences were found by disease-stage focus and validation strategy (all p > 0.05). Only five external test-set estimates contributed to the primary analysis; subgroup comparisons had limited precision. Conclusion Imaging AI models showed promising accuracy for AVNFH detection in research datasets. However, risk of bias, between-study heterogeneity, and limited external testing restrict confidence in their clinical applicability. Prospective, multicenter validation and evaluation of clinical benefit are needed before routine implementation.

title: Age- and sex-specific values of regional bone mineral density from opportunistic CT of the lower lumbar spine, pelvis, sacrum, and proximal femur.
abstract: Objective Standard osteoporosis assessment using dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) provides limited 2D measures (BMD, T-score), potentially missing localized bone density differences relevant to fracture risk. Opportunistic CT allows comprehensive 3D volumetric bone density analysis. This study presents a detailed 3D statistical model of CT-derived apparent volumetric bone mineral density (CT-vBMD) covering the L4 and L5 vertebrae, pelvic bones, sacrum, and proximal femur and examines spatial distributions and associations with age and sex. Materials and methods Retrospective analysis included 330 routine abdominal CT scans (ages 20-91; approximately balanced by sex). Bones were segmented with a semi-automated workflow, internally calibrated, registered to bone-specific population templates, and projected onto corresponding tetrahedral meshes. Whole-bone averages were compared across age groups and between sexes. For each element, we calculated mean vBMD, variability, correlations with age and sex, and cluster-defined low-density and age-sensitive subregions. Results The global spatial pattern was similar in females and males. The highest CT-vBMD values were localized mainly to cortical load-bearing zones, whereas the lowest values were concentrated in trabecular spongiosa. Older age was associated with lower whole-bone CT-vBMD in all bones and with stronger negative associations in trabecular-rich regions, such as the subchondral acetabulum, femoral neck, sacral ala, and vertebral bodies. Cortical-dominant load-bearing regions showed weaker negative associations with age. Conclusion This framework maps anatomically localized associations between age and CT-vBMD beyond the regions routinely assessed by DXA. Opportunistic CT mapping may complement standard osteoporosis assessment by providing spatial information for the pelvis, sacrum, lower lumbar spine, and proximal femur.

title: Regional variation in vertebral bone marrow adiposity: a population-based atlas of age- and sex-specific patterns.
abstract: Background Bone marrow adipose tissue (BMAT) is a metabolically active fat depot implicated in skeletal aging and systemic metabolism. While chemical shift-encoding MRI enables noninvasive quantification of bone marrow fat fraction (BMFF), current knowledge of vertebral BMAT is largely limited to small cohorts or restricted anatomical regions. Purpose To characterize the spatial distribution of vertebral bone marrow fat fraction across the spine and determine region-specific associations with age and sex in a population-based cohort. Materials and methods In this retrospective study, MRI data from 82,920 UK Biobank participants recruited between 2006 and 2010 were analyzed. The baseline case subset (n = 81,318) had a mean age of 54.8 ± 7.6 years, and 42,113/81,318 (51.8%) were female. Automated vertebral body segmentation enabled voxel-wise BMFF quantification using Dixon MRI. Vertebra- and region-level BMFF metrics were derived. Associations with age and sex were assessed using region-specific linear regression. Results Vertebral BMAT demonstrated a non-linear cranio-caudal pattern. Mean BMFF was ~ 39% in the cervical, ~ 55% in the thoracic, ~ 45% in the lumbar spine, and ~ 70% in the sacrum. BMAT increased with age in all regions (all p < 0.001; increase per decade: cervical 3.33%, thoracic 3.41%, lumbar 2.95%, sacral 3.83%). Females exhibited higher BMFF than males across all regions (all p < 0.001). The overall spatial pattern remained consistent across age groups and sexes. Conclusion Vertebral BMAT exhibits a structured, non-linear spatial distribution with region-specific age- and sex-dependent patterns. This population-based atlas provides normative reference data supporting region-specific BMAT assessment in skeletal and metabolic disease.

title: Dual-energy CT virtual non-calcium imaging for differentiating pathologic from non-pathologic femoral fractures: a study of inexperienced non-radiologist readers.
abstract: Objective To assess the effect of dual-energy CT (DECT) virtual non-calcium (VNCa) imaging on the ability of inexperienced non-radiologist readers to differentiate pathologic from non-pathologic femoral fractures. Materials and methods In this retrospective diagnostic accuracy study, 45 eligible emergency department patients with femoral fractures who underwent DECT between January 2022 and September 2024 were included, comprising 20 patients with pathologic fractures and 25 with non-pathologic fractures. The reference standard for fracture classification was established using surgical records or histopathologic results. Two inexperienced non-radiologist readers independently evaluated conventional CT alone and conventional CT combined with color-coded DECT VNCa images in separate reading sessions. Sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) were compared between the two sessions. AUCs were compared using the paired DeLong test. Results The addition of DECT VNCa significantly improved sensitivity for detecting pathologic fractures in both readers. For Reader 1, sensitivity increased from 65 to 95% (p = 0.031), and accuracy increased from 77.8% to 95.6%. For Reader 2, sensitivity increased from 50 to 85% (p = 0.016), and accuracy increased from 68.9% to 91.1%. Specificity remained high without significant differences between sessions. AUC increased from 0.765 (95% CI, 0.617-0.913) to 0.955 (95% CI, 0.883-1.0) for Reader 1 and from 0.670 (95% CI, 0.506-0.834) to 0.905 (95% CI, 0.802-1.0) for Reader 2 (p = 0.0135 and < 0.01, respectively). Conclusion Adding color-coded DECT VNCa to conventional CT improves the diagnostic performance of inexperienced non-radiologist readers in detecting pathologic femoral fractures.

AUC increased from 0.765 (95% CI, 0.617-0.913) to 0.955 (95% CI, 0.883-1.0) for Reader 1 and from 0.670 (95% CI, 0.506-0.834) to 0.905 (95% CI, 0.802-1.0) for Reader 2 (p = 0.0135 and < 0.01, respectively).

Conclusion

Adding color-coded DECT VNCa to conventional CT improves the diagnostic performance of inexperienced non-radiologist readers in detecting pathologic femoral fractures.

title: Clinical evaluation of deep learning-based acquisition and reconstruction techniques for accelerated 2D shoulder magnetic resonance imaging acceleration at 3 T.
abstract: Purpose GE has recently developed Sonic DL MRI acceleration technology. We wished to (1) quantify scanner time reduction compared to the AIR Recon DL already in clinical use at our institution and (2) preliminarily evaluate any change in diagnostic findings between these methods. Methods A total of 30 outpatients undergoing routine shoulder MRI for shoulder pain were recruited. Each underwent routine AIR Recon DL and Sonic DL exams containing the same sequences. Three subspecialized musculoskeletal radiologists assessed image quality, graded pathology, and reported diagnostic confidence in a blinded fashion. Differences in image quality and confidence were compared using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. Results Sonic DL reduced nominal acquisition time 38.7% compared to AIR Recon DL (6 min 15 s versus 10 min 12 s). Artifact was considered slightly worse on the routine examination (3.20 versus 3.37, P = 0.039); there was no significant difference in image quality, sharpness, or signal-to-noise ratio between routine and Sonic DL accelerated exams (P 0.171-0.861). Inter-reader agreement was broadly similar between routine-routine and routine-Sonic DL comparisons (median agreement 0.867 and 0.839, respectively). Within-reader analysis identified subacromial/subdeltoid bursitis and supraspinatus tendon tears more frequently on the routine protocol than on Sonic DL (P 0.049 and P 0.006, respectively). Conclusion Sonic DL enabled a 38.7% reduction in nominal shoulder MRI acquisition time with broadly comparable image quality and inter-reader agreement in this pilot cohort. Diagnostic equivalence was not established; subacromial/subdeltoid bursitis and supraspinatus tears were potentially less conspicuous on Sonic DL. A larger powered validation study would be needed to fully evaluate diagnostic performance.

title: A case report of pediatric Gardner syndrome and literature review.
abstract: This case report discusses the diagnosis and treatment of a 14-year-8-month-old male patient genetically diagnosed with Gardner syndrome (GS), systematically reviewing the disease's epidemiology, clinical manifestations, imaging advances, and management strategies. The patient presented with a post-influenza A chest wall mass and had prior resections of abdominal/scalp masses. Colonoscopy revealed > 20 adenomatous polyps. Imaging demonstrated multiple craniofacial osteomas and epidermoid cysts. Genetic testing identified a pathogenic APC gene mutation (NM_000038.6:c.4669_4670del (p.Ile1557*) heterozygous variant). GS, a familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP) subtype, has an estimated pediatric incidence of 1/8000-1/14,000. Its classic triad comprises colorectal polyps, osteomas, and soft tissue tumors. Recent studies indicate earlier malignant transformation of duodenal polyps in children versus adults, with desmoid tumor incidence reaching 10-20%. In imaging, low-dose CT, panoramic radiography, and contrast-enhanced MRI can improve early detection of bone lesions and soft tissue tumors. Genetic testing (APC/MUTYH) is the pediatric screening gold standard. Optimized chemoprevention (sulindac/celecoxib) and endoscopic monitoring have significantly improved prognoses. This case highlights the urgency of multidisciplinary management and genetic counseling for pediatric GS.

title: Primary leiomyosarcoma arising adjacent to a femoral stem following total hip arthroplasty: a case report with radiologic and histopathological correlation.
abstract: Periprosthetic sarcomas associated with total hip arthroplasty (THA) are exceedingly rare, and most reported cases represent undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma or osteosarcoma. Primary leiomyosarcoma of bone is also an uncommon malignancy, accounting for less than 1% of primary malignant bone tumors. The occurrence of primary leiomyosarcoma adjacent to an orthopedic implant is therefore exceptionally rare. A 69-year-old woman presented with progressive left thigh pain 13 years after THA. Radiographs demonstrated osteolysis and cortical thinning at the distal femoral stem. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed an intramedullary lesion with cortical thinning and contrast enhancement. 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography-CT showed increased uptake at the lesion (SUV max, 11.9), without evidence of other primary tumors. The differential diagnoses included implant-related osteolysis, infection, metastatic tumor, and primary bone tumor. An open biopsy was performed, and a diagnosis of pleomorphic sarcoma was made. Wide resection with proximal femoral replacement was performed. Histopathological examination established the diagnosis of primary leiomyosarcoma of bone. Prominent lymphocytic infiltration and immunohistochemical findings, including p53 overexpression and partial loss of Rb expression, within the tumor, raise the possibility of chronic inflammation and associated molecular alterations as theoretical contributing factors to tumorigenesis. Periprosthetic sarcomas can mimic more common postoperative complications, making diagnosis challenging. Delayed diagnosis may adversely affect prognosis. This case highlights the importance of considering malignancy in atypical periprosthetic lesions and underscores the role of multimodality imaging and biopsy in achieving an accurate diagnosis.

title: IgG4-related disease of the pelvic floor musculature mimicking neoplasm: a case report with imaging-pathologic correlation.
abstract: IgG4-related disease (IgG4-RD) is an immune-mediated fibroinflammatory condition that can form tumefactive mass-like lesions and mimic malignancy across organ systems. We describe a rare presentation involving the deep pelvic floor musculature with imaging-pathologic correlation while underscoring diagnostic pitfalls. A 49-year-old man with a history of systemic lupus erythematosus, night sweats, and left lower quadrant abdominal pain underwent CT of the abdomen and pelvis, which demonstrated a right posterior pelvic sidewall mass and retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy. Pelvic MRI demonstrated an ill-defined intramuscular mass centered in the right iliococcygeus and pubococcygeus muscles. Relative to skeletal muscle, the lesion demonstrated iso- to low T1 signal intensity, intermediate T2 signal intensity, restricted diffusion, and moderate, diffuse contrast enhancement, raising concern for neoplasm or an inflammatory process. Image-guided biopsy revealed fibrotic soft tissue with severe lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate and increased IgG4-reactive plasma cells. The IgG4+/IgG+ plasma cell ratio was > 75%, consistent with IgG4-RD when integrated with the clinical, laboratory, imaging and pathologic findings. IgG4-related disease with mass-like involvement of the pelvic floor musculature has not, to the best of our knowledge, been previously reported in the English literature. This entity can present as an ill-defined, enhancing, diffusion-restricting intramuscular mass and therefore may mimic a neoplastic process.

title: A rare case of bilateral cuboid-navicular coalitions.
abstract: Cuboid-navicular coalitions are an exceptionally rare form of tarsal coalitions, representing less than 1% of all tarsal coalitions. Although tarsal coalitions classically become symptomatic during adolescence, cuboid-navicular coalitions may remain clinically silent until adulthood and can present with nonspecific chronic midfoot or hindfoot pain. We present a rare case of bilateral cuboid-navicular coalitions in a 42-year-old man with progressive bilateral midfoot pain, associated degenerative hindfoot and midfoot changes, and bilateral peroneal tendon pathology. Initial management consisted of orthotics, bracing, and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, but symptoms progressed over 8 years. Cross-sectional imaging demonstrated bilateral cuboid-navicular coalitions, progressive degenerative changes, and high-grade right peroneus longus tear. The patient underwent excision of the right cuboid-navicular coalition, excision of the right lateral calcaneal tubercle with inferior peroneal retinacular release, and debridement and repair of the right peroneus longus and brevis tendons. This case highlights the importance of considering rare tarsal coalitions in adults with chronic nonspecific midfoot pain and emphasizes the value of MRI and CT for diagnosis, characterization of associated pathology, and operative planning.

title: AI-enhanced routine CT for opportunistic osteoporosis screening and risk assessment.
abstract: Osteoporosis-related fractures create a large and often preventable burden, yet many individuals undergoing CT for unrelated care do not receive skeletal assessment. This review evaluates artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled use of routine CT for opportunistic case-finding and risk assessment, with emphasis on the boundary between promising retrospective performance and safe clinical implementation. Automated vertebral segmentation and CT-derived bone-density estimation can reduce manual workload, and published diagnostic studies report high discrimination in selected cohorts. However, pooled estimates are heterogeneous because the reference standard, anatomical target, CT acquisition, reconstruction, contrast status, calibration method, prevalence, and validation design differ substantially across studies. These differences preclude a universal CT threshold or a universal minimum detector-row requirement; detector-row configuration should be considered together with the broader acquisition and reconstruction parameters. For implementation, AI should be deployed as a validated triage tool-not as a stand-alone diagnostic replacement for clinical assessment and indicated DXA/QCT. A credible pathway requires a defined CT-protocol eligibility check; pre-specified vertebral region of interest and exclusions; protocol- and contrast-aware quantification; scanner-specific quality assurance and calibration monitoring where applicable; external validation in representative populations; and an explicit route from an AI alert to confirmatory testing and treatment evaluation. AI may also enable concurrent vertebral-fracture and body-composition assessment, but clinical utility must be shown through downstream testing, treatment, fracture, workload, equity, and cost outcomes. The near-term priority is therefore not higher retrospective diagnostic performance alone, but reproducible, transparent, and prospectively evaluated integration into radiology workflows.

title: Percutaneous cryoablation of musculoskeletal tumours: the largest reported single-centre case series - outcomes, complications and subgroup analysis.
abstract: Objectives Cryoablation is an image-guided, minimally invasive treatment technique that uses extreme cold to induce tumour destruction. Its role in musculoskeletal oncology has expanded in recent years, although large clinical series remain limited. This study reports a large single-centre experience of percutaneous cryoablation for musculoskeletal tumours, including metastatic lesions, benign and cartilaginous tumours, and primary bone tumours. Materials and methods This was a single-centre retrospective cohort study conducted at a tertiary musculoskeletal oncology centre. All procedures were performed by a single specialist musculoskeletal interventional radiologist with over 20 years of experience. The study included patients who underwent percutaneous cryoablation for musculoskeletal tumours between June 2021 and December 2025. Clinical response, radiological response, recurrence, and complications were assessed over a median follow-up of 3 months (mean 8.7 months; range 0-48 months). Radiological response was assessed using pre-treatment and post-treatment Hounsfield Unit (HU) measurements on CT; this is not a validated radiological scoring system and is reported as a complementary, exploratory marker alongside standard clinical response assessment. Complications were graded using the CIRSE classification system. Results A total of 48 patients underwent percutaneous cryoablation during the study period. The cohort included 26 males and 22 females, with a median age of 40 years. A good or complete response was achieved in 28 patients, representing 58% of the total cohort. A partial response was achieved in seven patients, representing 15% of the total cohort. HU reduction was observed in 45 of 48 patients, representing 94% of the cohort. The overall complication rate was 6.3%, with three complications recorded among 48 procedures. No major complications or procedure-related deaths were observed. Conclusions Cryoablation appears to be a safe and effective minimally invasive treatment for selected musculoskeletal tumours. Most patients achieved a good, complete, or partial response, with a low complication rate. Hounsfield Unit reduction after treatment may provide a useful, though as yet non-validated, marker of radiological response. Further prospective studies with longer follow-up, standardised response criteria and validated complication grading are needed to confirm these findings.

title: Underreporting of sacroiliac joint structural abnormalities on routine abdominal CT in axial spondyloarthritis: a longitudinal workflow analysis.
abstract: Objective To quantify documentation of predefined, conspicuous sacroiliac joint (SIJ) structural abnormalities on routine abdominal CT in patients with established axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA) and identify associated factors. Materials and methods This retrospective longitudinal study evaluated 516 abdominal CT examinations from 188 patients with established SpA. Two readers applied a predefined hierarchical SIJ classification, with adjudication of disagreements. The primary analysis included 226 Moderate or Major examinations; all had fusion-based patterns. Patient-clustered logistic generalized estimating equations included workflow, request-level context, structural severity, prior recognition, and scan year. Results SIJ findings were absent from 152 of 226 reports (67.3%). Total fusion was unreported in 90 of 136 examinations (66.2%), including 83 of 129 with bilateral total fusion (64.3%). Crude non-reporting was 89.2% in acute care and 50.0% in rheumatology. The four-examination MSK-oriented subgroup was combined with rheumatology for modeling. Adjusted non-reporting was 82.7% in acute care and 50.6% in the combined MSK-pathway, a 32.1-point difference (95% CI, 6.2-52.0); the corresponding OR was 0.20 (95% CI, 0.05-0.75). Structural severity and request-level context were not independently associated with non-reporting. Conclusion Documentation of conspicuous SIJ structural abnormalities on routine abdominal CT was frequently absent and varied by workflow. Including a field for SIJ findings in structured abdominal CT reports may lead more radiologists to look for joint abnormalities. Automated detection requires external and prospective validation before clinical implementation.

title: Externally validated MRI radiomics machine learning models for differentiating between myxoid liposarcoma and myxoma.
abstract: Objective To develop and externally validate a radiomics-based machine learning model for differentiating myxoid liposarcoma (MLS) from myxoma on MRI and compare its diagnostic performance with that of experienced musculoskeletal radiologists. Methods In this retrospective study, T1-weighted and fluid-sensitive MRI sequences from 109 patients with histologically confirmed MLS or myxoma were used to train support vector machine (SVM), random forest (RF), and XGBoost (XGB) classifiers. Models were evaluated in an independent external cohort of 32 patients from a second institution using different scanner hardware and protocols. Diagnostic performance was compared with that of two fellowship-trained senior musculoskeletal radiologists. Secondary analysis assessed MLS grading. Results The T1-weighted SVM achieved the strongest external binary performance (accuracy, 0.84; AUC, 0.91), outperforming RF and XGB (p = 0.005 and p < 0.001, respectively). title: Intraarticular acetabular osteoid osteoma treated with CT-guided radiofrequency ablation after unsuccessful arthroscopy: a case report and literature review.
abstract: Acetabular osteoid osteoma is uncommon, and treatment can be difficult when the lesion is intraarticular or associated with osteoarthritis. We report a 17-year-old male with an intraarticular acetabular osteoid osteoma. The lesion was located in the medial portion of the acetabular fossa and was associated with synovitis, joint effusion, joint space narrowing, and osteophyte formation. Arthroscopy was initially selected for lesion resection and joint assessment. However, the medial location limited instrument access, preventing complete resection. The residual lesion was subsequently treated with CT-guided radiofrequency ablation (RFA) using a posterior osseous trajectory and intraarticular cooling with chilled 5% dextrose solution. At 4 weeks, hip pain had completely resolved, and MRI showed resolution of perilesional bone marrow edema. Pain relief persisted through 12 months without analgesic use. A literature review summarizes previous treatment approaches for acetabular osteoid osteoma. This case illustrates that treatment planning should account for lesion location, joint condition, and technical feasibility. CT-guided RFA may be useful when a safe percutaneous trajectory to the lesion can be planned.

title: The role of extracardiac radiotracer biodistribution in the evaluation of cardiac amyloidosis: a retrospective multicenter study on [99mTc]Tc-DPD and [99mTc]Tc-HMDP.
abstract: Bone scintigraphy using [99mTc]Tc-DPD or [99mTc]Tc-HMDP is a non-invasive cornerstone for diagnosing transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (ATTR-CA). However, their interchangeability and the clinical relevance of systemic extracardiac uptake (ExtCU) remain poorly defined. To systematically compare the diagnostic performance and whole-body biodistribution profiles of [99mTc]Tc-DPD and [99mTc]Tc-HMDP in patients with suspected cardiac amyloidosis (CA). We retrospectively evaluated a multicenter cohort of patients investigated for suspected CA who underwent late planar whole-body scintigraphy and targeted SPECT/CT with either radiotracer as part of their diagnostic workup. Inclusion required a final, confirmed diagnosis of ATTRwt, ATTRv, or AL amyloidosis. Myocardial visual Perugini score (VISUAL_PS) and systemic ExtCU (pulmonary, appendicular muscular, visceral, and miscellaneous) were recorded. The study included 224 patients (DPD: n = 109, comprising 70 ATTRwt, 20 ATTRv, 19 AL; HMDP: n = 115, comprising 90 ATTRwt, 13 ATTRv, 12 AL). In ATTRwt, the DPD cohort presented predominantly with Perugini Grade 2 (76%), whereas the HMDP cohort skewed toward Grade 3 (72%, p < 0.001). DPD was significantly associated with appendicular muscular uptake (ATTRwt: 84% vs. 38%, p < 0.001), creating a competitive "soft-tissue sink effect". Conversely, HMDP demonstrated a unique predilection for pulmonary retention (ATTRwt: 68% vs. 46%, p = 0.008; ATTRv: 61% vs. 10%, p = 0.006). Visceral uptake was rare in ATTR but was a robust negative predictor strongly favoring AL amyloidosis (OR 0.016, p < 0.001). [99mTc]Tc-DPD and [99mTc]Tc-HMDP possess distinct biodistribution profiles precluding direct interchangeability. HMDP maximizes myocardial contrast, whereas DPD provides a superior representation of the systemic musculoskeletal amyloid burden. Nuclear medicine physicians must adopt tracer-specific interpretive approaches to optimize non-invasive phenotyping. not applicable.

title: First-in-human dosimetry and biodistribution of [ 89 Zr]Zr-oxine-labeled autologous leukocytes using PET/CT.
abstract: Purpose Cell tracking with zirconium-89 PET has the potential for widespread clinical and research applications, including imaging infection and inflammation and tracking cell-based therapies. This prospective first-in-human clinical trial assessed the dosimetry and safety profile of [ 89 Zr]Zr-oxine-labeled autologous leukocytes in healthy female participants. Methods Four healthy adult female participants (ages 37-53) received 10.9 ± 2.9 MBq of [ 89 Zr]Zr-oxine-labeled autologous leukocytes and underwent whole-body PET/CT imaging at five time points (0, 4, 24, 48, and 72 h). Regions of interest were automatically segmented on CT using a machine learning-based approach and manually refined. Time-integrated activity coefficients were calculated using Simpson's rule, with physical decay assumed beyond the final time point. Mean absorbed-dose and effective-dose coefficients were estimated using OLINDA 2.1. Results Administration was well-tolerated among all participants. The highest mean absorbed-dose coefficients (mGy/MBq) with standard deviation were observed in the spleen (3.52 ± 1.38), liver (2.1 ± 0.45), adrenals (1.62 ± 0.24), uterus (1.48 ± 0.98), and kidneys (1.36 ± 0.12). The mean effective-dose coefficient was 0.92 ± 0.06 mSv/MBq, numerically lower than the predicted value of 1.14 mSv/MBq based on the distribution of [ 111 In]In-oxine-labeled leukocytes in adult females (P = 0.006, one-sample t-test). The use of [ 89 Zr]Zr-oxine-labeled leukocytes enabled the visualization of leukocyte distribution and temporal dynamics. Conclusion This study demonstrates the safety and favorable dosimetry of [ 89 Zr]Zr-oxine-labeled leukocytes in healthy humans. These results support the further use of this approach for imaging autologous leukocytes using PET in a range of clinical and research settings. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03807973. Registered January 16, 2019.

title: Diagnostic performance of multiparametric model integrating ¹⁸F-MFBG PET/CT imaging parameters and clinical factors for differentiating neuroblastoma from ganglioneuroblastoma: a preliminary study.
abstract: Purpose To develop and preliminarily validate a multiparametric diagnostic model integrating ¹⁸F-meta-fluorobenzylguanidine (¹⁸F-MFBG) PET/CT imaging parameters with clinical factors for noninvasive differentiation of neuroblastoma (NB) from ganglioneuroblastoma (GNB) in pediatric patients. Methods This retrospective study enrolled 42 pediatric patients with histologically confirmed NB (n = 23) or GNB (n = 19) who underwent ¹⁸F-MFBG PET/CT prior to treatment. Quantitative imaging parameters and clinical data were extracted. Correlations were assessed using Spearman's rank correlation coefficient. Multicollinearity among predictors was evaluated using variance inflation factors (VIF). Univariate and multivariable Firth logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent predictors. The discriminative performance of the model was evaluated via receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, the DeLong test, bootstrap validation, net reclassification improvement (NRI), and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI). Results SUVmax, SUVmean, TBRmean, TBRmax, AUC-CSH and TL-hNET differed significantly between NB and GNB(P < 0.05). Severe multicollinearity (VIF > 10) was observed among imaging parameters, SUVmax was selected for multivariable modeling, along with age, bone metastasis and 11q23 deletion as the strongest clinical predictors. In the multivariable Firth model, SUVmax (OR = 8.665; P = 0.029) and age (OR = 0.676; P = 0.043) remained independently associated with NB. Bone metastasis showed a trend toward independent association with NB (OR = 11.753; P = 0.050), with the association approaching statistical significance. Three diagnostic models were constructed and compared: (1) imaging-only model (SUVmax); (2) clinical-factor model (age + bone metastasis); and (3) integrated model (SUVmax + age + bone metastasis). The combined model achieved an AUC of 0.856(95%CI:0.737-0.975), showing a trend toward improved discrimination compared with both the SUVmax-only model (AUC = 0.810, 95%CI:0.668-0.952) and the clinical-factor model (AUC = 0.787, 95%CI:0.659-0.916). Bootstrap validation (2000 resamples) and IDI analysis provided supportive evidence of incremental value of the integrated model (Combined vs. SUVmax-only: IDI = 0.122, P = 0.014; Combined vs. clinical: IDI = 0.083, P = 0.045). Conclusion The multiparametric model integrating ¹⁸F-MFBG PET/CT imaging parameters with clinical factors generated a promising preliminary hypothesis for diagnostic performance for differentiating NB from GNB, pending rigorous external validation in larger, multicenter cohorts.

title: ¹⁸F-sodium fluoride PET/CT as a complementary measure of osteoblastic disease burden in axial spondyloarthritis: a prospective exploratory study.
abstract: Purpose To determine whether SIJ ¹⁸F-NaF uptake is associated with MRI-defined inflammation and structural damage and whether it provides a complementary measure of osteoblastic disease burden. Methods In this prospective exploratory study, 43 adults with chronic low back pain underwent pelvic radiography, sacroiliac joint (SIJ)-MRI, and whole-body ¹⁸F-NaF PET/CT and were classified as having radiographic axial spondyloarthritis or ankylosing spondylitis (AS; n = 29), non-radiographic axial spondyloarthritis (nr-axSpA; n = 5), or degenerative joint disease (DJD; n = 9). MRI was evaluated using SPARCC inflammation and structural scores. SIJ uptake was assessed visually and quantified using SUVmax. The primary endpoint was the correlation between SIJ SUVmax and the SPARCC structural score. Results SIJ SUVmax correlated with the SPARCC inflammation (ρ = 0.629) and structural (ρ = 0.606) scores (both p < 0.001) on SIJ-MRI; both associations persisted after mutual adjustment. Median SIJ SUVmax differed across AS, nr-axSpA, and DJD (14.7 [11.2-22.4], 5.5 [4.4-9.9], and 5.7 [4.0-9.2], respectively; p = 0.001). Visually positive uptake occurred in 23/29 (79.3%) patients with AS, including 10/16 without MRI-defined bone marrow edema; no patient with AS had edema without increased uptake. Peripheral joint and entheseal uptake were frequent but non-discriminatory. Exploratory AUCs were 0.841 for AS versus DJD and 0.848 for AS versus nr-axSpA. Conclusion SIJ ¹⁸F-NaF uptake was associated with both MRI-defined inflammation and structural burden in patients with AS, including those without active inflammation on MRI. SIJ SUVmax warrants evaluation as a complementary quantitative imaging biomarker of osteoblastic disease burden, but all derived thresholds require external validation.

title: Imaging of mass-forming intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma: from detection to personalized treatments.
abstract: Mass-forming intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (MF-iCCA) represents the most frequent phenotype of intrahepatic CCA in Europe, yet its insidious clinical onset and tendency toward late presentation translate into a poor prognosis, with only 20-30% of patients eligible for curative resection. In this context, imaging plays a pivotal role, spanning from initial lesion detection and characterization to staging, treatment selection, and response assessment. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) constitute the backbone of diagnostic workup, with complementary strengths: CT offers superior spatial resolution for vascular assessment, while MRI, enhanced by diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) and hepato-biliary phase sequences, provides higher sensitivity for intrahepatic staging and tumor delineation. Contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) serves as a valuable adjunct for differential diagnosis. Accurate resectability assessment requires careful evaluation of vascular involvement, future liver remnant (FLR) volume, and metastatic spread, with 18 F-FDG-PET playing an incremental role in nodal staging. In the era of personalized therapy, including chemo-immunotherapy, targeted agents, and locoregional treatments, functional response criteria beyond RECIST 1.1 are increasingly essential. A thorough knowledge of expected post-treatment imaging appearances is critical to avoid misclassification of treatment effects as disease progression. This narrative review aims to provide a comprehensive, imaging-focused overview of MF-iCCA, covering its radiological features and differential diagnosis, the role of imaging in staging and resectability assessment, imaging-based criteria guiding personalized treatment selection, and expected post-treatment imaging findings.

title: Diagnostic performance of [ 18 F]-FDG or [ 68 Ga]-FAPI PET/MRI for nodal assessment in colorectal cancer: a retrospective comparative analysis.
abstract: Purpose The evaluation of lymph node metastasis in colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a critical challenge, as it significantly impacts prognosis and treatment decisions. PET/MRI with various tracers may take advantages of MRI together with the functional imaging of PET. This study aims to evaluate the diagnostic performance of PET/MRI for lymph node metastasis of CRC in a real-world clinical cohort and to explore the imaging characteristics of PET/MRI using [ 18 F]-FDG or [ 68 Ga]-FAPI tracers. Methods This retrospective study included 51 patients with confirmed colorectal cancer who underwent PET/MRI imaging ([ 18 F]-FDG or [ 68 Ga]-FAPI) between March 2020 and December 2022. The choice of PET tracer was determined according to clinical indication and tracer availability. The N stage and lesion status (N0 vs. N + and positive node vs. negative node) were independently evaluated by two nuclear medicine physicians. ROC curve analysis was performed using histopathological results and clinical follow-up as the reference standards. Results The accuracy for nodal (N) status assessment was 91.4% for PET/MRI and 85.7% for MRI. PET/MRI showed numerical higher diagnostic performance than MRI for detecting lymph node metastases (AUC 0.88 vs. 0.81; p = 0.19). At the region-based lymph node level, PET/MRI demonstrated significantly higher accuracy (93.6% vs. 87.8%, p = 0.002), specificity (98.9% vs. 92.5%, p = 0.01), and positive predictive value (85.7% vs. 40.0%, p = 0.002). In the exploratory analysis of [ 68 Ga]-FAPI subgroup, no false-positive regional findings were observed, corresponding to a specificity of 100% (50/50; 95% CI, 92.9%-100%). It also showed numerical higher SUV max and TBR compared to [ 18 F]-FDG PET/MRI, although the differences were not statistically significant (4.35 vs. 2.25, p = 0.64; 17.4 vs. 5.65, p = 0.29). Among 11 patients who underwent a watch-and-wait or local excision strategy under PET/MRI surveillance, 1 experienced local regrowth and 1 developed lung metastasis. No nodal recurrence was observed during follow-up. Conclusion PET/MRI demonstrated encouraging diagnostic accuracy and high specificity in evaluating lymph node metastasis in colorectal cancer. These findings support further investigation of PET/MRI as part of multimodal imaging strategies for CRC management, particularly in patients considered for organ preservation.

title: CT radiomics and topology-based intratumoral heterogeneity for preoperative prediction of nuclear β-catenin expression in hepatocellular carcinoma.
abstract: Background Nuclear β-catenin accumulation reflects activation of the Wnt/β-catenin pathway in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but noninvasive preoperative prediction of this immunohistochemical phenotype remains incompletely established. Purpose To develop and externally validate CT radiomics and topology-based intratumoral heterogeneity (ITH) models for preoperative prediction of nuclear β-catenin expression in HCC. Materials and methods This multicenter retrospective study included 1029 patients with histopathologically confirmed HCC. Patients from two participating institutions formed the development cohort and were split into training (n=620; nuclear β-catenin-positive, 293) and internal validation (n=267; nuclear β-catenin-positive, 126) sets. Patients from an independent third institution formed the external validation cohort (n=142; nuclear β-catenin-positive, 43). Whole-tumor portal venous phase CT radiomics features and topology-based ITH features were extracted from the audited image-mask cohort. Model discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility were evaluated using AUC, bootstrap 95% confidence intervals, calibration summaries, Brier scores, and decision curve analysis. Results In external validation, AUCs were 0.677 for the clinical model, 0.862 for the radiomics model, 0.857 for the ITH model, 0.831 for the core ITH model, 0.863 for the radiomics-ITH model, and 0.886 for the stacking model. Compared with radiomics alone, stacking showed a numerical ΔAUC of 0.024 (95% CI, -0.010 to 0.060; P=0.180). Conclusion CT radiomics and topology-based ITH features showed external predictive value for nuclear β-catenin expression in HCC. The stacking model had the highest external AUC, but its improvement over radiomics alone was not statistically significant. If prospectively validated, these CT-based approaches could complement tissue assessment for pretreatment biological stratification.

title: Machine learning-assisted monitoring of radiofrequency ablation in hepatic tumors using spectral traces.
abstract: Purpose Accurate intraoperative assessment of radiofrequency ablation (RFA) margins in hepatic malignancies remains a significant clinical challenge. Methods This study investigates the efficacy of hyperspectral imaging (HSI) for objective, spatially resolved discrimination of ablated tissue, viable tumor, and normal parenchyma in 10 ex vivo liver specimens. Analysis of visible-near-infrared (VNIR) reflectance revealed distinct spectral signatures, characterized by a consistent monotonic hierarchy (ablated < normal < tumor), enabling reliable tissue differentiation. Segmentation performance was systematically evaluated using four supervised classifiers: Spectral Angle Mapper (SAM), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), and Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA). The total delineated tissue area exhibited notable inter-method variability, ranging from 137,283 to 189,289 pixels (+ 37.9%), underscoring sensitivity to classifier architecture. Results Nevertheless, all approaches maintained biologically coherent tissue distributions, with normal parenchyma predominating (44-56%), followed by tumor (25-39%) and ablated regions (17-20%). That is consistently indicating the necessity for monitoring ablative margins. SAM, SVM, and LDA classifiers achieved class-specific detection errors around 3.5% and 18%. LDA attained the highest overall accuracy (94.5%), demonstrating the potential of HSI for reliable, intraoperative image-guided tissue characterization. Dimensionality reduction across 462 spectral bands identified an optimal discriminative window within 643-698 nm, supporting the development of streamlined multispectral systems. Conclusion Overall, HSI is neither a contact nor destructive modality for quantitative RFA assessment. Despite classifier-dependent variability necessitating standardized or ensemble strategies, these findings support its prospective integration into real-time surgical guidance, pending in vivo validation.

title: Peritumoral ultrasound-driven multimodal AI model for predicting lymphovascular space invasion and prognosis in cervical cancer.
abstract: Purpose Accurate preoperative assessment of lymphovascular space invasion (LVSI) in cervical cancer (CC) remains challenging despite its importance for treatment planning and risk stratification. This study aimed to develop and evaluate a hybrid model integrating peritumoral ultrasound radiomics features, deep learning features, and clinical data for preoperative prediction of LVSI in CC. Additionally, we assessed the model's prognostic value for disease-free survival (DFS) and explored LVSI-associated molecular pathways using data from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA). Methods In a retrospective cohort (n = 241) and a prospective cohort (n = 51), radiomics features were extracted from tumor and peritumoral regions of interest on ultrasound images. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression and machine learning classifiers generated a radiomics score (Rad-score). Simultaneously, transfer learning with pre-trained convolutional neural networks constructed a deep learning score (DL-score). A hybrid model integrating clinical factors, Rad-score, and DL-score was developed. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the curve (AUC). Furthermore, prognostic value (Kaplan-Meier analysis), model interpretability using Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP), and biological pathways were assessed. Results Overall, 292 women were included: 188 in the training set, 53 in the internal validation set, and 51 in the prospective testing set. The hybrid model achieved the highest performance (AUC: 0.79, 95%CI: 0.66-0.92; sensitivity: 0.85, 95%CI: 0.71-0.98) in the prospective testing set, outperforming the single-modality models. Exploratory survival analysis showed shorter DFS in the high-risk group (P < 0.05). SHAP analysis identified the DL-score as the primary predictor. Biologically, the Wnt/β-catenin pathway was significantly enriched in LVSI-positive patients. Conclusions The hybrid model, evaluated in a prospective cohort, showed potential for preoperative LVSI prediction and DFS risk stratification in CC. TCGA analysis showed Wnt/β-catenin enrichment in LVSI-positive tumors, providing complementary biological context. Further validation in larger independent multicenter cohorts is needed before clinical application.

title: Machine learning-based CT radiomics for identifying high risk esophageal varices of bleeding in hepatocellular carcinoma.
abstract: Purpose Esophageal variceal (EV) bleeding is a lethal complication in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Current risk stratification relies on invasive endoscopy or systemic surrogates of liver cirrhosis. This study aimed to develop a machine learning model utilizing EV-specific CT radiomics to identify high-risk esophageal varices, as defined by endoscopic criteria, in patients with HCC. Methods 151 HCC patients were enrolled and divided into a training cohort (n = 101; 75 high-risk; January 2017 - December 2022) and an independent temporal validation cohort (n = 50; 29 high-risk; January 2023 - December 2024). Endoscopic stigmata were used as an endpoint, including active bleeding or varices with high-risk features. Radiomic features were extracted from contrast-enhanced CT images acquired within six months prior to endoscopy. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the curve (AUC) of receiver operating characteristic (ROC), Brier score, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Results In the training cohort, the varix-specific radiomics signature developed via the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) demonstrated excellent discriminative power (cross-validated AUC: 0.956; 95% CI 0.872-1.000). In the temporal validation cohort, this model maintained high generalizability, yielding an AUC of 0.926 (95% CI 0.846-0.984, sensitivity: 93.1%, specificity: 71.4%) as well as a Brier score of 0.1186 and good calibration (intercept = -0.157, slope = 1.354). Surface-to-Volume Ratio (SVR) and NGTDM Coarseness are feasible radiomics. Conclusion The varix-specific radiomics model provides highly sensitive and mathematically stable non-invasive risk stratification for EV bleeding in patients with HCC.

title: Preoperative FDG PET/CT topographic patterns and clinical parameters are associated with incomplete cytoreduction in peritoneal carcinomatosis: proposal of the Resectability Score.
abstract: Purpose To explore associations between preoperative FDG PET/CT-derived topographic patterns, clinical variables, and unfavorable surgical outcome (incomplete cytoreduction or intraoperative unresectability) in peritoneal carcinomatosis (PC), and to propose a simple, transparent, preoperatively applicable Resectability Score (RS) as a hypothesis-generating tool for future prospective validation. Methods In this single-center retrospective cohort study (May 2018-April 2026), 39 patients with histopathologically confirmed PC who underwent surgical exploration were included. Univariable associations between PET/CT variables (PET-estimated Peritoneal Cancer Index [PCI] category, mesenteric root uptake, retroperitoneal uptake) and clinical factors and the composite endpoint were assessed. Given the limited number of outcome events, no multivariable model was fitted. The RS was proposed conceptually, with weights reflecting the strength of the observed associations, and its performance was deliberately not assessed in this dataset. Results Eighteen of 39 patients (46.2%) had an unfavorable outcome (CC-2/3, n = 12; intraoperative unresectability, n = 6). PET-estimated PCI > 20 (OR 9.4, 95% CI 2.0-44.3; p = 0.003), mesenteric root FDG uptake (0/21 vs. 6/18; p = 0.006), and retroperitoneal FDG uptake (0/21 vs. 6/18; p = 0.006) were significantly associated with unfavorable outcome; gastric primary tumor showed a non-significant trend (OR 4.8, 95% CI 1.0-22.3; p = 0.07). Among 33 patients who underwent CRS + HIPEC, complete cytoreduction rates by PET-estimated PCI category were 85.7% (PCI ≤ 10), 63.6% (PCI 11-20), and 25.0% (PCI > 20) (p = 0.017). All six unresectable patients had shown mesenteric root or retroperitoneal FDG uptake preoperatively. Conclusion Preoperative FDG PET/CT topographic patterns in particular high disease burden and mesenteric root or retroperitoneal uptake are associated with unfavorable surgical outcomes in PC. The proposed RS is a hypothesis-generating tool only; formal derivation, internal validation, and external validation are required before any clinical application.

To explore associations between preoperative FDG PET/CT-derived topographic patterns, clinical variables, and unfavorable surgical outcome (incomplete cytoreduction or intraoperative unresectability) in peritoneal carcinomatosis (PC), and to propose a simple, transparent, preoperatively applicable Resectability Score (RS) as a hypothesis-generating tool for future prospective validation.

Methods

In this single-center retrospective cohort study (May 2018-April 2026), 39 patients with histopathologically confirmed PC who underwent surgical exploration were included. Univariable associations between PET/CT variables (PET-estimated Peritoneal Cancer Index [PCI] category, mesenteric root uptake, retroperitoneal uptake) and clinical factors and the composite endpoint were assessed. Given the limited number of outcome events, no multivariable model was fitted. The RS was proposed conceptually, with weights reflecting the strength of the observed associations, and its performance was deliberately not assessed in this dataset.

Results

Eighteen of 39 patients (46.2%) had an unfavorable outcome (CC-2/3, n = 12; intraoperative unresectability, n = 6). PET-estimated PCI > 20 (OR 9.4, 95% CI 2.0-44.3; p = 0.003), mesenteric root FDG uptake (0/21 vs. 6/18; p = 0.006), and retroperitoneal FDG uptake (0/21 vs. 6/18; p = 0.006) were significantly associated with unfavorable outcome; gastric primary tumor showed a non-significant trend (OR 4.8, 95% CI 1.0-22.3; p = 0.07). Among 33 patients who underwent CRS + HIPEC, complete cytoreduction rates by PET-estimated PCI category were 85.7% (PCI ≤ 10), 63.6% (PCI 11-20), and 25.0% (PCI > 20) (p = 0.017). All six unresectable patients had shown mesenteric root or retroperitoneal FDG uptake preoperatively.

Conclusion

Preoperative FDG PET/CT topographic patterns in particular high disease burden and mesenteric root or retroperitoneal uptake are associated with unfavorable surgical outcomes in PC. The proposed RS is a hypothesis-generating tool only; formal derivation, internal validation, and external validation are required before any clinical application.

title: Deep learning-based detection of pneumoperitoneum on computed tomography: performance and clinical feasibility.
abstract: Purpose Early detection of pneumoperitoneum on computed tomography (CT) is critical because delayed diagnosis of gastrointestinal perforation is associated with increased morbidity and mortality. We evaluated the diagnostic performance and clinical applicability of a deep learning model for automated pneumoperitoneum detection on CT. Methods In this retrospective diagnostic accuracy study, CT scans for 263 patients with surgically confirmed gastrointestinal perforation and 78 normal controls from a single tertiary center (January 2010-September 2024) were included. Positive CT scans were divided into training, validation, internal test, and temporally independent external test datasets, with 78 normal controls included in the external test dataset. Free air was manually segmented and verified by surgical and radiological experts. A segmentation-based deep learning model was developed using the no-new-Segment Anything Model (nnSAM) framework and compared with a conventional no-new-Net (nnUNet) model. Segmentation and classification performance were assessed on internal and temporally independent external test datasets. Result In the internal test dataset (n = 43 positive cases), the nnSAM model achieved a higher detection rate (97.7% vs. 90.7%) and significantly higher mean Dice similarity coefficient (0.739 ± 0.266 vs. 0.684 ± 0.283; p = 0.045) than the nnUNet one. In the external test dataset, nnSAM also showed a higher detection rate in positive cases (97.9% vs. 85.4%) and a significantly higher mean Dice similarity coefficient (0.863 ± 0.189 vs. 0.746 ± 0.208; p = 0.003). Conclusion The performance advantage of nnSAM was particularly evident in small-volume pneumoperitoneum cases. The nnSAM-based model showed improved accuracy and robustness for pneumoperitoneum detection on CT, supporting its potential as a clinically useful decision-support tool for emergency radiology workflows and triage of patients with suspected gastrointestinal perforation.

title: DCE-MRI histogram analysis for predicting survival in patients with epithelial ovarian carcinoma.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate the potential of dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI (DCE-MRI) histogram analysis for predicting overall survival (OS) in epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) patients. Methods This retrospective study included 155 patients with EOC who underwent pretreatment DCE-MRI. Histogram features extracted from DCE-MRI parametric maps were selected using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) Cox regression, with selection stability assessed across 200 bootstrap replicates. Clinical, imaging, and combined models were developed using Cox regression and random survival forest (RSF). Apparent concordance indices (C-indices) were calculated and corrected for optimism using 100 bootstrap resamples with fixed predictor sets. Exploratory Kaplan-Meier analyses assessed risk-group separation, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis was used for model interpretation. Results Median OS was 54 months. The 10th percentile of K trans was selected in 88.0% of bootstrap replicates. Imaging Cox and RSF models achieved apparent C-indices of 0.790 and 0.827, respectively. Combined models incorporating this feature, International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO) stage, and residual disease status achieved apparent C-indices of 0.806 for Cox regression and 0.853 for RSF, respectively. Bootstrap-corrected C-indices were higher for the combined than the corresponding clinical models, with a statistically significant improvement for Cox regression (0.805 vs. 0.737, P = 0.020) but not for RSF (0.810 vs. 0.745, P = 0.120). The combined models did not differ significantly (P = 0.820). Exploratory Kaplan-Meier analysis using cohort-specific median risk-score cutoffs showed significant OS separation (both P < 0.001). The 10th percentile of K trans yielded the highest mean absolute SHAP value in the combined Cox model and exhibited the widest distribution of SHAP values in the combined RSF model. Conclusion DCE-MRI histogram features, particularly the 10th percentile of K trans , may aid OS prediction in EOC and provide complementary prognostic information when integrated with clinicopathological factors. These exploratory findings require prospective multicenter external validation.

title: Routine CT reporting of vascular involvement in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma: completeness and association with margin-positive resection.
abstract: Background National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) guidelines emphasize detailed reporting of tumor-vessel relationships for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), but the completeness and prognostic significance of vascular findings documented in routine clinical CT reports remain uncertain in the contemporary era of neoadjuvant therapy (NAT). Purpose To assess the completeness of NCCN-relevant vascular reporting in routine preoperative CT examinations and determine whether CT-reported vascular findings and derived NCCN resectability categories are associated with margin-positive (R1) resection. Materials and methods In this retrospective single-center study, 528 patients who underwent resection for pathologically confirmed PDAC between 2011 and 2026 were identified. For each patient, the most recent preoperative staging CT report and corresponding surgical pathology report were linked. Tumor-vessel relationships involving the superior mesenteric artery (SMA), celiac axis, common hepatic artery (CHA), superior mesenteric vein (SMV), and portal vein (PV) were extracted from routine clinical reports via a large language model, which underwent validation against 2 readers. Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate associations between vascular findings, NCCN resectability category, and R1 resection after adjustment for age, sex, tumor size, tumor location, and NAT status. Results Among 528 patients (mean age, 69.2 years ±9.9; 277 men), 257 (48.7%) received NAT and 172 (32.6%) had R1 resection. Complete reporting of all five NCCN vessels was present in 224/528 (42.4%) reports. NCCN resectability category could be assigned in 322 patients, including 150 (46.6%) resectable, 123 (38.2%) borderline resectable, and 49 (15.2%) locally advanced tumors. R1 rates increased progressively across categories (26.7%, 45.5%, and 53.1%, respectively; p < 0.001). After adjustment, SMA abutment (OR, 2.85; p = 0.001), SMA encasement (OR, 2.49; p = 0.023), celiac encasement (OR, 2.81; p = 0.021), CHA encasement (OR, 2.31; p = 0.031), PV abutment (OR, 2.31; p = 0.007), and SMV encasement (OR, 2.50; p = 0.014) were independently associated with R1 resection. In sensitivity analysis assuming unreported vessels had no tumor contact, borderline resectable tumors (OR, 2.68; 95% CI, 1.60-4.50) and locally advanced tumors (OR, 4.77; 95% CI, 2.22-10.23) demonstrated progressively higher odds of R1 resection relative to resectable tumors. Conclusion Complete NCCN-compliant vascular reporting was uncommon in routine PDAC CT reports, limiting standardized resectability classification. Nevertheless, CT-reported vascular findings and NCCN resectability categories derived from routine reports retained significant associations with margin-positive resection, supporting the continued clinical relevance of vascular staging information communicated in everyday radiology practice.

title: Predicting advanced-stage recurrence in resected hepatocellular carcinoma using preoperative gadoxetic acid-enhanced MRI radiomics.
abstract: Objectives To develop and validate a preoperative gadoxetic acid-enhanced MRI-based radiomics model for predicting the time to advanced-stage recurrence in patients undergoing resection for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Materials and methods This retrospective single-center study included patients with Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer (BCLC) stage 0/A HCC who underwent resection between 2009 and 2014. Patients were temporally divided into training (n = 272; 2009-2011) and validation (n = 210; 2012-2014) cohorts. Time to advanced-stage recurrence was defined as the interval from resection to macrovascular invasion and/or extrahepatic metastasis. Two radiologists segmented tumors on hepatobiliary phase images, followed by 3-mm peritumoral expansion and propagation to co-registered dynamic T1- and T2-weighted images. After extraction of Image Biomarker Standardization Initiative-compliant features, a radiomics model was developed using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO)-Cox regression. Model performance and inter-reader reproducibility of binary risk stratification were evaluated using the concordance index (C-index) and Cohen's kappa, respectively. Results Five-year advanced-stage recurrence occurred in 15% of the training (42/272) and validation (32/210) cohorts. In the validation cohort, the radiomics model yielded a C-index of 0.716 (95% CI, 0.631-0.801). This outperformed the preoperative BCLC (0.597; 95% CI 0.551-0.644) and Hong Kong Liver Cancer (0.594; 95% CI 0.516-0.672) staging systems, and was equivalent to the postoperative clinicopathological model (0.716; 95% CI 0.626-0.807). Radiomic-based risk stratification showed good inter-reader reproducibility (kappa = 0.757). Conclusion The preoperative radiomics model outperformed staging systems and was comparable to the postoperative clinicopathological model in predicting advanced-stage recurrence, relying entirely on noninvasive data.

title: Development and validation of a preoperative CT-based radiomics nomogram for predicting postpancreatectomy acute pancreatitis after pancreatoduodenectomy.
abstract: Purpose To investigate the value of radiomics based on preoperative contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CECT) for predicting postpancreatectomy acute pancreatitis (PPAP) after pancreatoduodenectomy (PD). Methods A retrospective analysis included 104 patients who underwent PD and preoperative CECT between May 2019 and March 2025. Patients were randomly divided into training (n = 73) and test (n = 31) sets at a 7:3 ratio. PPAP was defined according to the biochemical and radiologic components of the International Study Group for Pancreatic Surgery (ISGPS) criteria. After pancreatic parenchyma delineation, radiomics feature extraction and selection, an optimal model was developed on the training set to calculate the radiomics score (rad-score). Independent clinical and morphological features were selected by univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses. Conventional quantitative CT attenuation ratios of the pancreatic parenchyma were also evaluated. Predictive performance was assessed by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. Results PPAP occurred in 41 patients. Four models were compared: a clinical-morphologic model (age and main pancreatic duct [MPD] dilation), a conventional model (age, MPD dilation and arterial-to-portal ratio [A/P]), a radiomics model (rad-score alone), and a radiomics-integrated model (age, MPD dilation and rad-score). The radiomics-integrated model achieved the highest area under the curve (AUC) among the four models, with the AUC of 0.854 (95% CI 0.758-0.951) in the training set and 0.862 (95% CI 0.732-0.993) in the test set. Conclusion The radiomics-integrated model demonstrated promising performance for preoperative prediction of PPAP after PD, which may facilitate individualized risk stratification and perioperative management.

title: Photon counting detector CTA for prostate arterial evaluation during the workup for prostate artery embolization.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate small field of view (FOV) ultra-high spatial resolution pelvic photon-counting detector prostate CT angiograms (UHR PCD CTA) for identifying prostate arterial anatomy and extraprostatic anastomoses in patients undergoing workup for prostate artery embolization (PAE). Methods IRB-approved retrospective imaging and electronic medical record review of men who consecutively underwent UHR PCD CTA for PAE workup at our institution from 8/1/2022 to 12/1/2024. UHR PCD CTAs were evaluated by two vascular and interventional radiologists for main and accessory candidate prostatic arteries (PA/s) and anastomoses to penile, bladder, or rectal arteries. A main PA was defined as supplying the central gland and an accessory PA was defined as supplying the peripheral zone. PAs were categorized using the Carnevale classification. In patients who proceeded to PAE, digital subtraction angiograms (DSA) were retrospectively compared with UHR PCD CTA findings. Results UHR PCD CTA was obtained prior to PAE consultation for 50 men. We evaluated 100 pelvic sides, identifying 180 candidate PAs with a median of 3 candidate PAs per patient (mean, 3.6; range, 2-7). Overall, 56% (101/180) of candidate PAs were main and 44% (79/180) were accessory. Abridged Carnevale classifications: Type 5-21% (38/180). Eight accessory candidate PAs arose from the superior rectal artery. At least one candidate anastomosis arose from 40% (72/180) of candidate PAs. Of 95 total candidate anastomoses, 69 were extraprostatic (30 rectal, 20 bladder, 19 penile) and 26 were intraprostatic collaterals; 56% (53/95) arose from accessory and 44% (42/95) from main candidate PAs. Twenty-eight of 50 (56%) men underwent PAE, during which 72% (74/103) of available candidate PAs were selected, and prostatic supply was confirmed by DSA in 100% (74/74) of selected vessels. Conclusion Small FOV UHR PCD CTA is useful in identifying candidate PA supply, as well as potential extraprostatic anastomoses, providing an arterial roadmap for PAE planning. Candidate PA supply was confirmed by DSA in all selected vessels among patients who proceeded to PAE.

title: Deep learning reconstruction in prostate MRI: technical principles, clinical applications, and future directions.
abstract: Multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI) has become integral to the detection, localization, risk stratification, and management of prostate cancer. Increasing utilization of prostate MRI in screening, active surveillance, targeted biopsy guidance, and treatment planning has amplified the demand for faster imaging protocols while maintaining high diagnostic quality. Conventional MRI acceleration strategies, including parallel imaging and compressed sensing, improve acquisition efficiency but remain limited by trade-offs involving signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), image sharpness, artifacts, and reconstruction complexity. Deep learning reconstruction (DLR) has emerged as a promising artificial intelligence-based approach for MRI acceleration and image enhancement. Unlike traditional reconstruction methods that rely primarily on predefined mathematical models, DLR uses neural networks to learn image priors and reconstruction features from MRI data. Published studies suggest that DLR may enable accelerated acquisitions while maintaining or, in some settings, improving image quality through denoising, artifact reduction, and improved spatial resolution and lesion conspicuity. However, these effects vary according to the reconstruction algorithm, sequence, acceleration factor, and clinical setting. Variational networks combine physics-based MRI constraints with learned regularization and represent an important framework for DLR. In prostate MRI, available studies have reported substantial reductions in acquisition time for T2-weighted and diffusion-weighted imaging while generally maintaining perceived image quality. Reported benefits include improved lesion conspicuity, reader confidence, and delineation of anatomic structures. Current evidence suggests that DLR generally preserves PI-RADS assessment and diagnostic performance rather than systematically altering lesion categorization; however, evidence demonstrating improvements in diagnostic accuracy or clinical outcomes remains limited. Important limitations include vendor and algorithm dependence, potential reconstruction artifacts, variability in quantitative imaging metrics, limited multicenter validation, and uncertain generalizability across scanners, protocols, and clinical settings. This review summarizes the technical principles underlying DLR, discusses current clinical applications in prostate MRI, highlights representative studies and workflow implications, reviews limitations, and outlines future directions for this rapidly evolving technology.

title: Associations between tissue stiffness, tumor response to transarterial chemoembolization and prognosis in hepatocellular carcinoma: insights from multifrequency 3D-magnetic resonance elastography.
abstract: Objectives To investigate the correlation between tissue stiffness, as measured across various target tissues using multifrequency three-dimensional magnetic resonance elastography (3D-MRE), and tumor responses to transarterial chemoembolization (TACE), as well as post-treatment prognosis in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Methods HCC patients scheduled for TACE treatment were prospectively recruited and received multifrequency 3D-MRE before the initiation of TACE procedure. Measurements of tumor stiffness (TS), liver stiffness (LS), and spleen stiffness (SS) were conducted at frequencies of 60 Hz and 30 Hz, respectively. Treatment response was assessed using the mRECIST. Patient follow-up was conducted to evaluate overall survival outcomes. Results The final patient cohort consisted of 43 patients (mean age: 56.66±10.13 years; 34 males), including 16 non-responders and 27 responders. Non-responders exhibited significantly elevated TS (4.10±2.54 vs. 2.68±1.61kPa, p=0.035), LS (2.88±1.43 vs. 1.97±0.59kPa, p=0.026), and SS (4.03±0.90 vs. 3.13±1.08kPa, p=0.008) at the frequency of 30Hz. Firth's penalized univariable logistic analysis identified age (adjusted odds ratio [OR]=0.93, P=0.036), tumor number (OR=0.69, P=0.035), LS at 60Hz (OR=0.79, p=0.046), TS at 30Hz (OR=0.73, p=0.037), LS at 30Hz (OR=0.44, p=0.008), and SS at 30Hz (OR=0.44, P=0.009) as potential predictors of treatment response. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve for predicting treatment response was 0.69 for age, tumor number and TS at 30Hz, 0.67 for LS at both 60Hz and 30Hz, and 0.75 for SS at 30Hz. Univariable Cox regression identified TS at both 60Hz (hazard ratio=1.15, p=0.014) and 30Hz (hazard ratio=1.40, p=0.010) as potential predictors of overall survival. Conclusion Spleen stiffness measured at 30 Hz via 3D-MRE may serve as a potential predictor of treatment response to TACE in HCC patients, whereas tumor stiffness measured at both 60Hz and 30Hz appears to correlate with overall survival. Further research is necessary to validate these preliminary associations.

title: CT assessment of colonic laterality in situs inversus and situs ambiguus: a multicenter retrospective study.
abstract: Purpose To characterize proximal and distal colonic laterality and appendiceal-base location on CT in patients with situs inversus and situs ambiguus. Methods This retrospective multicenter study included 79 patients identified from abdominal CT reports at three tertiary hospitals between December 2003 and March 2025 (70 with situs inversus; 9 with situs ambiguus). A radiologist assessed thoracoabdominal organ arrangement, proximal and distal colonic laterality, combined proximal-distal colonic laterality pattern, and appendiceal-base location. The end of the cecum was used when the appendiceal base was not visible. Distributions of colonic laterality between the two situs types were compared using exact tests. Results In situs inversus, the proximal colon was left-sided in 66/70 patients (94.3%; 95% CI, 86.2-97.8), the distal colon was right-sided in 67/70 (95.7%; 95% CI, 88.1-98.5), and a left-proximal/right-distal combined colonic pattern occurred in 64/70 (91.4%; 95% CI, 82.5-96.0). The appendiceal base or cecal surrogate was in the left lower quadrant in 61/70 (87.1%; 95% CI, 77.3-93.1). In situs ambiguus, the proximal colon was midline-crossing in 7/9 patients (77.8%; 95% CI, 45.3-93.7), and the distal colon was left-sided in 6/9 (66.7%; 95% CI, 35.4-87.9). Locations of the appendiceal base or cecal surrogate were distributed across all abdominal regions. Distributions of segmental and combined colonic laterality differed between situs inversus and situs ambiguus (all exact p < .001). Conclusion Situs inversus usually shows mirror-image colonic laterality and a left-lower-quadrant appendiceal base, but exceptions occur. In this cohort, situs ambiguus showed greater variability. Colonic laterality and appendiceal-base location should be directly assessed on CT rather than inferred from situs classification alone.

title: Limited incremental value and cross-cohort transferability of CT radiomics for survival prediction after TACE in hepatocellular carcinoma.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate whether pretreatment CT radiomics adds information for overall survival (OS) prediction among patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) treated with transarterial chemoembolization (TACE), and assess frozen imaging-model performance in an independent cohort. Methods This retrospective study included 221 WAW-TACE and 98 HCC-TACE-SEG patients with pretreatment arterial and portal venous CT. Incremental value of a tumor-radiomics Random Survival Forest score (R1) beyond cohort-specific clinical Cox models (C0) was evaluated within each cohort using 5-fold cross-validation repeated 10 times. External validation was restricted to frozen WAW-trained R1 models (Top-K = 5, 10, 15) applied to HCC-TACE-SEG without refitting; the combined C0 + R1 model was not externally validated. Results WAW-TACE included 162 deaths and HCC-TACE-SEG 86 deaths. In WAW-TACE, C0, R1 Top-K = 15, and C0 + R1 achieved C-indices of 0.646 ± 0.043, 0.593 ± 0.049, and 0.639 ± 0.045, respectively. Corresponding HCC-TACE-SEG estimates were 0.496 ± 0.087, 0.530 ± 0.072, and 0.495 ± 0.094. Thus, R1 did not consistently improve cohort-specific clinical reference models. In frozen external application, Top-K = 5, 10, and 15 achieved C-indices of 0.463 (95% CI 0.397-0.532), 0.535 (0.468-0.608), and 0.528 (0.460-0.598), respectively. Conclusion The evaluated models showed no consistent incremental value for OS prediction within these TACE cohorts and limited frozen-model discrimination in the clinically distinct HCC-TACE-SEG cohort. These findings do not support clinical use of these models or establish a general limitation of CT radiomics.
