title: CT imaging features in prognostic risk stratification compared to clinical staging in resectable gastric cancer: a multicenter study.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate the incremental prognostic value of visually assessable CT features beyond clinical stage (cStage) for disease-free survival (DFS) risk stratification in gastric cancer. Methods Patients undergoing curative gastrectomy were retrospectively included in development and external cohorts. Clinical and pathological stages were reconstructed according to the AJCC 8th edition and simplified to three tiers. Clinical Stage, CT Imaging, and Combined models were evaluated for discrimination, calibration, bootstrap-corrected performance, and external validation. Incremental prognostic value was assessed using changes in the C-index and time-dependent AUCs. A development-derived CT Imaging Score (CIS) cutoff was locked for exploratory risk refinement within preoperative cStage strata. Results Among 886 patients (development, n = 698; external, n = 188), cStage-pStage concordance was 51.0% and 61.2%, respectively (linear-weighted κ = 0.387 and 0.513). In the development cohort, adding CIS to cStage increased the C-index from 0.648 to 0.805 (ΔC-index = 0.160, P = 0.002) and the 1-, 3-, and 5-year AUCs by 0.159, 0.184, and 0.193, respectively (all P = 0.001). The optimism-corrected C-index was 0.797 for the Combined model. External C-indices were 0.676, 0.694, and 0.695 for the Clinical Stage, CT Imaging, and Combined models, respectively. In the development cohort, CIS-high status was associated with worse DFS within cStage II (HR = 8.66, 95% CI: 5.59-13.42) and cStage III (HR = 5.78, 95% CI: 3.74-8.92), with associations retained after adjustment for postoperative pStage. Conclusion Integrating visually assessable CT imaging features with conventional cStage improved DFS prognostic discrimination in the development cohort, while the derived CIS further refined risk stratification within preoperative cStage groups.

title: FDG PET/MR for liver metastases: a systematic review and meta-analysis of diagnostic accuracy and technical protocols with a proposed reporting framework.
abstract: Purpose This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the diagnostic performance of FDG PET/MR for detecting hepatic metastases from extrahepatic primary malignancies, together with acquisition protocols, reconstruction parameters, and technical heterogeneity. Methods A systematic search was conducted through September 2026. Eligible studies evaluated FDG PET/MR for hepatic metastases and reported diagnostic performance data and/or technical protocol information. Summary estimates of sensitivity and specificity were obtained using a bivariate random-effects model. A structured qualitative assessment of PET and MR acquisition, reconstruction parameters, and image interpretation strategies was also performed. Results Fifteen studies involving 861 patients met the inclusion criteria. Eight studies (53%) provided sufficient data for the diagnostic accuracy meta-analysis, whereas all contributed to the qualitative technical assessment. The meta-analysis demonstrated a summary sensitivity estimate of 0.94 (95% CI, 0.89-0.97) and a summary specificity estimate of 0.99 (95% CI, 0.92-1.00) for detecting hepatic metastases. Sensitivity showed substantial between-study heterogeneity (I² = 0.83), whereas specificity showed low heterogeneity (I² = 0.21). Technical assessment revealed marked variability in PET acquisition, MR protocols, reconstruction parameters, and reporting, with frequent underreporting of voxel size, filtering, and motion correction. Hepatobiliary contrast agents were used in only a minority of studies, and dedicated PET motion correction was rarely implemented. Conclusion FDG PET/MR demonstrates high lesion-level diagnostic accuracy for the detection of hepatic metastases, with high summary sensitivity and specificity. However, substantial between-study variability in sensitivity, together with variability and frequent underreporting of technical parameters, highlights the need for standardized acquisition protocols and reporting frameworks to improve reproducibility, comparability, and clinical translation.

title: An interpretable contrast-enhanced CT-based cross-attention transformer model for predicting progression-free survival in muscle-invasive bladder cancer: a multicenter study.
abstract: Background Patients with muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) typically have a dismal prognosis, even after undergoing radical cystectomy (RC). To address this limitation, we constructed and evaluated a preoperative deep learning (DL) model that leverages computed tomography (CT) imaging to stratify MIBC patients according to their risk of postoperative disease progression. Methods Data from MIBC patients undergoing RC at one of four institutions were retrospectively analyzed and allocated to training and validation cohorts. A dual-channel information fusion DL model was developed to predict the postoperative risk of progression according to preoperative CT images. Subsequently, a DL-based clinical signature was created by combining clinical features with the DL-derived score. The concordance index (C-index) and area under the curve (AUC) were used to evaluate the DL model's predictive capability, which was compared with the DL-based clinical signature, a clinical model, and a Ki67 model. Results In the retrospective cohort of 427 patients with MIBC, the DL score demonstrated favorable predictive performance for disease progression in the validation cohort (C-index: 0.774; AUC: 0.785), and generally showed higher predictive performance than the comparator models in the validation cohort. Using an optimal threshold, the patient cohort was categorized into two distinct subgroups, high-risk and low-risk, with differences in the cumulative incidence of progression observed between the two groups, supporting the model's ability to stratify patients according to progression risk. Conclusions The utilization of preoperative CT imaging in a DL framework enabled PFS prediction and risk stratification in patients with MIBC, with potential value for individualized postoperative surveillance.

title: Structured MRI reporting for deep pelvic endometriosis: objective report quality and surgeon-perceived clinical utility in a randomized comparative study.
abstract: Objectives To compare structured and free-text MRI reporting in terms of objective report quality and surgeon ratings of perceived clinical utility in suspected deep pelvic endometriosis. Materials and methods In this single-center randomized reader study, 20 radiology residents were assigned to free-text or structured reporting. Five residents became unavailable before report generation and provided no outcome data. The remaining 15 readers completed the same 22 pelvic MRI examinations, generating 330 reports: 154 free-text and 176 structured reports. Reports were compared with an imaging reference standard established by two pelvic radiologists through independent review and consensus adjudication. The primary endpoint was clinically weighted completeness. Secondary endpoints included unweighted completeness, explicit negative discrepancies relative to the expert imaging reference, positive findings unsupported by the expert imaging reference, and reporting time. Objective outcomes were analyzed using mixed-effects models or Poisson generalized estimating equations. In an exploratory paired assessment, two expert gynecologic surgeons evaluated 44 reports, comprising one free-text and one structured report for each MRI examination. Results Structured reporting was associated with an 8.1%-point increase in completeness compared with free-text reporting (95% CI, 4.1-12.1; p < 0.001) and a 5.6%-point increase in clinically weighted completeness (95% CI, 1.3-10.0; p = 0.011). Reporting time was 4.52 min longer with structured reporting (95% CI, 3.05-5.99; p < 0.001). Structured reporting was also associated with more explicit negative discrepancies relative to the expert imaging reference (rate ratio, 2.94; 95% CI, 1.73-4.98; p < 0.001). These discrepancies were mainly explicit compartment-based negative statements. In the exploratory surgeon assessment, structured reports received higher ratings for perceived completeness, usefulness for clinical decision-making, and adequacy to clinical needs, whereas clarity ratings were similar between formats. Conclusion Structured MRI reporting was associated with higher objective completeness and, in an exploratory assessment, higher surgeon ratings for several dimensions of perceived clinical utility. These findings should be balanced against longer reporting time and more explicit negative discrepancies relative to the expert imaging reference.

title: MRI-based deep learning model for prediction of Ki-67 expression level in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.
abstract: Background Ki-67 expression is a valuable prognostic indicator in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA). This study aimed to develop a non-invasive Deep learning (DL) model based on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and clinical data to predict Ki-67 expression preoperatively. Methods Patients with iCCA between January 2020 and January 2024 were retrospectively reviewed. Based on immunohistochemistry, patients were classified into high-expression group (Ki-67 > 50%) and low-expression group (Ki-67 ≤ 50%). After image acquisition, tumor segmentation, and preprocessing, a 3D-ResNet10 network was utilized for MRI feature extraction. A feed-forward neural network (FFN) was used for clinical feature extraction. Subsequently, the extracted image and clinical features were fused and fed into a lightweight classifier to perform Ki-67 level prediction. The performance of the DL models was evaluated via 5-fold cross-validation using accuracy, precision, sensitivity, specificity, F1-score, and the area under the curve (AUC). Results A total of 117 patients were ultimately included (30 cases in the high-expression group and 87 cases in the low-expression group). The model based solely on clinical variables demonstrated limited predictive efficacy (mean AUC: 53.18 ± 14.60%). The model utilizing MRI features alone exhibited high specificity (86.14 ± 10.25%) but modest sensitivity. In contrast, the fused DL model significantly outperformed both individual models, attaining a mean AUC of 84.24 ± 8.82%, an accuracy of 87.17 ± 5.95%, a specificity of 93.07 ± 9.35%, and a markedly improved sensitivity of 70.00 ± 19.44%, yielding a robust F1-score of 73.42 ± 12.28%. Conclusions We developed and validated a non-invasive DL model integrating contrast-enhanced MRI and clinical parameters that accurately predicts Ki-67 expression in iCCA, demonstrating superior diagnostic performance.

title: Contrast-enhanced CT-based multimodal modeling for overall survival prediction after resection of retroperitoneal liposarcoma: a bicentric retrospective study.
abstract: Objective Postoperative risk estimation in retroperitoneal liposarcoma (RPLS) remains challenging because conventional clinicopathologic models capture only part of its biological heterogeneity. We aimed to develop and externally evaluate a postoperative prognostic model integrating preoperative CT features with postoperative clinicopathologic information to estimate overall survival (OS) after RPLS resection. Materials and methods This bicentric retrospective study included 367 patients who underwent complete RPLS resection between 2009 and 2021. Institution 1 provided the training cohort (n = 128) and internal validation cohort (n = 55); Institution 2 provided the external test cohort (n = 184). A radiomics signature was constructed from three-dimensional tumor features. A deep-learning signature was derived from the largest axial tumor section using an ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-101 trained with Cox partial-likelihood loss. Clinical variables underwent univariable and multivariable Cox regression analysis. The retained clinicopathologic variables and imaging signatures were integrated into a combined model termed RDCS. Results During follow-up, 71, 30, and 107 patients died in the training, internal validation, and external test cohorts, respectively. The corresponding RDCS C-indices were 0.775, 0.704, and 0.725, each higher than those of the individual radiomics, deep-learning, and clinical models. Calibration curves showed agreement between predicted and observed survival. Decision-curve analysis suggested potential clinical utility within the evaluated thresholds. In a separate exploratory comparison in the external primary-tumor subset (n = 82), C-indices were 0.746 for RDCS and 0.590 for the official Sarculator application. Conclusion RDCS estimates OS after complete RPLS resection using preoperative CT-derived imaging signatures and postoperative clinicopathologic information. RDCS may complement established postoperative prognostic tools, but its application in surveillance and clinical management requires prospective validation and clinical impact assessment.

title: Imaging classification of pancreatic cystic lesions: a radiologist's guide.
abstract: Pancreatic cystic lesions (PCLs) are increasingly encountered in clinical practice owing to the widespread use of high-resolution cross-sectional imaging. These lesions comprise a heterogeneous group of entities ranging from benign cysts to pre-malignant neoplasms and invasive cancers, making accurate characterization essential for appropriate patient surveillance and therapeutic management. Imaging plays a pivotal role in lesion detection, differential diagnosis, and assessment of malignant potential. This review presents a practical imaging-based classification of PCLs founded on lesion morphology, relationship to the pancreatic ductal system, enhancement patterns, and associated imaging features. Using a stepwise diagnostic approach, pancreatic cystic lesions are categorized according to their increasing risk of malignancy into non-neoplastic cysts, serous cystic neoplasms, mucinous cystic lesions, and cystic degeneration of solid pancreatic tumors. Characteristic imaging findings, relevant differential diagnostic considerations, and imaging features associated with increased malignant potential are comprehensively reviewed, with particular emphasis on the role of MRI and MR cholangiopancreatography (MRCP) in lesion characterization. A structured pattern-recognition flowchart is proposed to facilitate routine image interpretation and enhance diagnostic confidence. In addition, a practical reporting template is presented to promote standardized assessment and effective communication within multidisciplinary teams. Emerging techniques, including diffusion-weighted imaging, quantitative MRI biomarkers, radiomics, artificial intelligence, and molecular analysis of cyst fluid, are discussed as promising tools for improving diagnostic accuracy and refining risk stratification. By emphasizing readily recognizable imaging features and a systematic diagnostic workflow, this review provides radiologists with a practical and clinically applicable framework for the evaluation, diagnosis, risk assessment, and multidisciplinary management of pancreatic cystic lesions.

title: Musculoskeletal oncology practice in Latin America: Workforce characteristics, resource availability, and territorial disparities.
abstract: Purpose Musculoskeletal oncology requires highly specialized, multidisciplinary care. Although the subspecialty has evolved worldwide, information on workforce characteristics, resource availability, and practice patterns across Latin America remains limited. Methods A cross-sectional survey using convenience sampling was conducted among orthopaedic surgeons involved in musculoskeletal oncology throughout Latin America. An adapted version of a previously published questionnaire was distributed through the Latin American Society of Musculoskeletal Tumors (SLATME) and professional networks. The survey explored training background, clinical practice characteristics, perceived support from selected specialties and specialized resources, perceived professional challenges, and treatment preferences. We performed descriptive analyses and comparisons by practice-location population size (< 1 million versus ≥ 1 million inhabitants). Results A total of 147 surgeons from 17 countries participated. Most respondents reported formal orthopaedic oncology training (76%) and academic orteaching involvement (93%). Respondents practicing in locations with ≥ one million inhabitants were significantly more likely to report treating ≥ 30 cases annually of soft tissue sarcoma (47% vs. 14%, p < 0.001), metastatic bone disease (73% vs. 40%, p < 0.001), and primary bone sarcoma (29% vs. 9%, p = 0.013). Access to molecular genetic testing, bone banks and allografts, and tumour reconstruction prostheses was also significantly greater in larger population centers, whereas access to MRI, radiotherapy, and intensive care did not differ significantly between groups. Conclusion Among survey respondents, musculoskeletal oncology practice in Latin America was characterized by high rates of specialized training and academic or teaching involvement. However, differences in the reported annual numbers of new malignant tumour cases treated and in access to advanced resources were observed according to practice-location population size. Because this study used a convenience sampling strategy, these findings reflect the respondents' practices but should not be generalized to the entire Latin American musculoskeletal oncology community.

title: A CAD-Based Workflow for Structured Mid-Sagittal Plane Definition in Contralateral Mandibular Mirroring: A Technical Note.
abstract: Objectives To describe a structured CAD-based workflow for defining the mandibular mid-sagittal plane during contralateral mirroring for unilateral mandibular defects and to demonstrate its clinical applicability in reconstructive planning. Methods DICOM data were segmented to generate a mandibular STL model. In CAD software, a mid-sagittal splitting plane was constructed using convergent geometric references, including a best-fit plane, principal inertia axis, and centre-of-gravity point, combined with pogonion as the anterior midline reference. The unaffected hemimandible was mirrored across this plane, exported as an STL file, and used for biomodel fabrication, guide planning, and reconstruction plate pre-contouring. A representative ameloblastoma case was used to illustrate the workflow. Results The workflow produced a mirrored mandibular template suitable for digital-to-physical transfer. In the representative case, the template supported preoperative reconstruction plate adaptation and intraoperative contour planning. At 12-month follow-up, facial contour and occlusion were clinically acceptable on qualitative assessment. Conclusions A convergent reference CAD workflow offers a practical method for standardising mid-sagittal plane definition in mandibular contralateral mirroring. The workflow may reduce reliance on subjective landmark selection in unilateral pathology; however, quantitative validation against established midplane methods is required. Clinical significance This technique provides a stepwise digital planning workflow for unilateral mandibular reconstruction, helping surgeons define the mid-sagittal plane, create mirrored templates, fabricate biomodels, and pre-contour reconstruction plates when tumour-related distortion limits reliable anatomical reference points. title: A Next-Generation Approach to Subglandular Breast Augmentation Using B-Lite Implants: The Feather Touch Technique.
abstract: Background Awake subglandular breast augmentation offers rapid recovery but requires effective perioperative analgesia. This study evaluated a standardized multilayer fascial plane anesthetic protocol for Feather Touch technique. Methods In this prospective study, 66 women underwent primary subglandular breast augmentation between January and November 2025 under light intravenous sedation with ultrasound-guided interpectoral, pectoserratus, serratus anterior, and subcutaneous infiltration. Results All procedures were completed without conversion to general anesthesia. Early recovery was uneventful in most patients. Four minor postoperative events were recorded: double-bubble deformity, bottoming out, palpable margins, and superior malposition. No major complications occurred. Lightweight implants were associated with improved early positional stability. Conclusions A standardized multilayer fascial plane protocol can be safely integrated into awake subglandular breast augmentation using the Feather Touch technique. Matching anesthetic delivery to subglandular dissection supports intraoperative comfort and early recovery, while implant weight may influence early stability. Level of evidence iv Breast Surgery. title: A Clinical Algorithm for Gynecomastia: From Diagnosis to Surgical Management.
abstract: Background Gynecomastia is a heterogeneous disorder spanning the full pediatric-to-adult age range; however, comprehensive single-institution analyses that integrate endocrine, comorbid, drug-related, and surgical perspectives within one framework remain limited. We characterized the demographic and etiologic landscape of gynecomastia in a large retrospective cohort, propose a practical diagnostic algorithm derived from these patterns, and summarize the institutional experience with surgical management. Methods We retrospectively reviewed all male patients with an electronic-medical-record diagnosis of gynecomastia at two tertiary academic hospitals between January 2011 and March 2026. True gynecomastia was confirmed clinically and, where indicated, by ultrasonography, mammography, or magnetic resonance imaging. Patients were categorized by primary etiology (physiologic, drug- or substance-induced, endocrine, pathologic systemic, or idiopathic) using a standardized diagnostic workflow, and surgical candidates were graded according to the Simon classification. Results Of 754 patients screened, 562 met criteria for true gynecomastia (pediatric ≤ 17 years, 30 [5.3%]; adult ≥18 years, 532 [94.7%]; mean age 58.7 ± 19.8 years; median 64, range 0-95). Bilateral disease accounted for 75.9% of patients with documented laterality. Idiopathic disease was the largest category (362; 64.4%), followed by drug- or substance-induced disease (135; 24.0%), pathologic systemic disease (43; 7.7%; predominantly chronic liver and kidney disease), endocrine disorders (13; 2.3%), and overt physiologic gynecomastia (6; 1.1%). Spironolactone (71 patients; 52.6% of drug-induced cases) and antiandrogen / androgen-deprivation therapy agents (28; 20.7%) jointly accounted for nearly three quarters of drug-induced disease. Etiologic distribution differed markedly by age: physiologic and idiopathic causes predominated in adolescents, whereas drug-induced disease rose sharply from the fifth decade onward and accounted for ≈26-29% of cases in patients aged 50-80 years. Forty-three patients (7.7%) underwent surgical correction (mean age 33.7 ± 18.9 years), most commonly for long-standing persistent disease or cosmetic and psychosocial indications; surgical conversion was substantially higher in idiopathic (9.3%) than in drug-induced (2.2%) or systemic pathologic disease (2.3%). Histopathology confirmed benign glandular hyperplasia in all 43 surgical specimens; no occult male breast carcinoma or other malignant tissue was identified (0 of 43), and patients with male breast carcinoma at initial presentation were excluded a priori. Conclusions Across a 15-year cohort, idiopathic and drug-induced disease (chiefly spironolactone and antiandrogen-class agents) accounted for nearly 90% of adult cases. A stepwise algorithm based on examination, medication review, and selective endocrine and radiologic testing classified etiology in routine practice, and surgery matched to Simon grade remained the definitive treatment for long-standing, severe, or psychosocially distressing disease. title: Morphological Patterns of Fibrous-Dominant Dorsocervical Humps and a Mesh Technique for the Diffuse Subtype.
abstract: Background Fibrous-dominant dorsocervical humps remain a challenging surgical condition because dense collagen structure limits the effectiveness of conventional liposuction and adjunctive energy-based techniques. Current surgical decision-making lacks an objective framework based on the internal structural organization of fibrosis. Objective To characterize CT-based morphological patterns of fibrous-dominant dorsocervical humps and to introduce a Mesh release technique specifically designed for the diffuse fibrous subtype. Methods Preoperative axial computed tomography (CT) images from 102 patients were reviewed to evaluate the internal morphology of fibrous tissue. Two distinct patterns were identified: a localized (mass-dominant) fibrous subtype and a diffuse (septal-dominant) fibrous subtype. Diffuse cases underwent three-dimensional CT reconstruction to further characterize the spatial architecture of fibrous septa. Accordingly, a minimally invasive Mesh release technique was developed to achieve multidirectional, cross-plane disruption of the diffuse fibrous network. Clinical outcomes were evaluated using a 4-point esthetic grading scale, and complications were recorded. Results Among 102 patients, 65 (63.7%) demonstrated the diffuse fibrous subtype and underwent the Mesh release technique. CT demonstrated widespread fibrous septa without a central fibrous mass, and three-dimensional reconstruction revealed an interconnected, multi-planar fibrous network. The mean operative time was 64.6 ± 12.3 min, and the mean aspirate volume was 269.1 ± 40.9 mL. Good-to-excellent contour improvement was achieved in 90.8% of patients. Postoperative complications occurred in 23.1% of patients, including transient numbness and seroma. Conclusions Preoperative CT distinguishes localized and diffuse fibrous subtypes of fibrous-dominant dorsocervical humps. For the diffuse fibrous subtype, the Mesh release technique enables effective cross-plane disruption of the fibrous network while achieving favorable contour restoration. title: Buttock Surgery: Key Insights, Challenges, and Best Practices-A Scoping Review.
abstract: Introduction Gluteal contouring encompasses diverse surgical and minimally invasive approaches, but technique selection and safety depend on anatomy, patient characteristics, and the quality of a heterogeneous evidence base. Methods This scoping review was conducted from January 2024 through June 2025 and reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR. PubMed and Embase were searched from inception through June 2025. Two reviewers independently screened records and charted data using a predefined form; disagreements were resolved by a senior author. Eligible sources addressed gluteal anatomy, indications, operative or injectable techniques, perioperative care, complications, or safety. Results The searches identified 938 records, and 44 sources were included. Evidence ranged from anatomical studies and technical reviews to case series, systematic reviews, and safety guidance. The mapped evidence supports individualized planning, subcutaneous-only fat grafting with ultrasound visualization, and cautious implant plane selection. Fat grafting had lower aggregate complication rates than implants in comparative reviews but retained the risk of fatal embolism when performed in unsafe planes. Evidence for fillers and several lifting or flap techniques was limited and heterogeneous. Conclusions Safe gluteal contouring requires anatomy-based planning, procedure-specific patient selection, and adherence to contemporary safety measures. Ultrasound guidance strengthens control of the fat injection plane, whereas the relative superiority of submuscular versus intramuscular implants remains uncertain. Higher-quality comparative studies with standardized outcomes are needed. title: Bilateral Ultrasound-Guided Erector Spinae Plane Block versus Serratus Anterior Plane Block for Postoperative Analgesia in Breast Reduction Surgery: A Prospective, Randomized, Outcome Assessor- Blinded, Controlled Trial.
abstract: Background Breast reduction surgery is a common aesthetic procedure associated with significant postoperative pain. Effective analgesia plays an important role in reducing opioid consumption, minimizing adverse effects, facilitating postoperative recovery, and improving patient satisfaction. Fascial plane blocks have recently gained popularity for breast surgery. This randomized study aimed to compare the effects of bilateral erector spinae plane block (ESPB) and serratus anterior plane block (SAPB) on postoperative analgesia in patients undergoing breast reduction surgery. Methods Seventy female patients undergoing bilateral breast reduction surgery were randomly allocated into two groups: ESPB (Group ESPB, n = 35) and SAPB (Group SAPB, n = 35). Blocks were performed bilaterally under ultrasound guidance, with 20 mL of 0.25% bupivacaine each side, 30 min before surgery. All procedures were performed using the wise-pattern reduction mammoplasty technique with a superiomedial pedicle by the same surgical team. Postoperative analgesia included intravenous paracetamol, ibuprofen, and intravenous tramadol patient-controlled analgesia (PCA). Primer outcome was 24-h tramadol consumption through intravenous patient-controlled analgesia (PCA). Secondary outcomes included time to first analgesic requirement from PCA, postoperative pain scores (NRS), intraoperative remifentanil consumption, perioperative variables, length of hospital stay, and adverse effects. Results Primary-outcome data were available for 35 SAPB and 34 ESPB patients. Mean 24-hour tramadol consumption was 70.0 ± 37.7 mg with SAPB and 53.2 ± 29.1 mg with ESPB (mean difference, SAPB minus ESPB, 16.8 mg; 95% confidence interval, 0.5-33.0 mg; p = 0.043). Median time to first analgesic requirement was 420 min with SAPB and 630 min with ESPB (log-rank p < 0.001). Pain scores did not differ significantly. Nausea occurred in five SAPB patients and no ESPB patients (Fisher's exact p = 0.054); vomiting occurred in either group. Bradycardia occurred in one ESPB group patient (p = 1). Conclusions In this single-center trial, ESPB was associated with lower 24-h tramadol consumption and a longer time to first PCA demand than SAPB, while pain scores were comparable. title: Technique, Safety and Adoption of Genicular Artery Embolization for Knee Osteoarthritis: A Nationwide Analysis of the German Quality-Assurance Registry.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate the nationwide adoption of genicular artery embolization (GAE) in Germany and to describe patient selection, technique, safety and radiation dose. Materials and methods We retrospectively analyzed procedures recorded in the quality-assurance registry of the German Society for Interventional Radiology and Minimally Invasive Therapy (DeGIR), from January 2024 to December 2025. Technical success, entered per procedure, was defined as subjective adequate devascularization of the synovial blush. Complications were graded using the modified CIRSE classification, and radiation exposure was expressed as dose-area product (DAP) and fluoroscopy time. The analysis was primarily descriptive. Results Overall, 2335 procedures in 2209 patients across 109 centers in 15 federal states were recorded (median age 67 years, IQR 59-77; 57% female; prior total knee arthroplasty (TKA) in 300, 13%). Annual volume rose from 579 procedures in 2024 to 1,756 in 2025, and the embolic agent shifted from permanent (40-21%) toward temporary microspheres (4-29%). Center-reported technical success was 93% (87% in 2024, 94% in 2025). Eleven complications were recorded (0.5%), all CIRSE grade 1-3, with no permanent sequelae; none were recorded in 2024. Median DAP was 1536 cGy cm 2 (IQR 731-3048) and median fluoroscopy time 24 min (IQR 16-34). Conclusion During rapid nationwide adoption, GAE was performed for osteoarthritis-related and post-TKA pain with low radiation dose and high center-reported technical success across centers of all volumes, supporting its feasibility in routine practice. The complication rate is a lower limit, as the registry is not designed for complication surveillance.
